manualTranslations.zh: 其辭曰：或問曹子曰：「夫寶以含珍為貴，士以藏器為峻，麟以絕跡標奇，松以負霜稱雋，是以蘭生幽澗，玉輝於仞。
manualTranslations.literal: Its words said: Someone asked Master Cao, "Treasure is prized for holding gems within; the gentleman is lofty for concealing his vessel; the qilin is marked extraordinary by leaving no tracks; the pine is called surpassing for bearing frost—thus orchids grow in secluded ravines, jade gleams from a thousand-foot cliff.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The piece opens with a question put to Master Cao: "A treasure is valued for the gem it holds; a gentleman is esteemed for the talent he keeps within; the qilin is famed for leaving no trace; the pine is praised for standing through frost. Orchids flourish in hidden streams; jade shines from towering cliffs.

manualTranslations.zh: 故子州浮滄瀾而龍蟠，吳季忽萬乘以解印，虞公潛崇岩以頤神，梁生適南越以保慎，固能全真養和，夷跡洞潤，陵冬揚芳，披雪獨振也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus Zizhou floated on the blue waves and coiled like a dragon; Wu Jihu suddenly cast off ten thousand chariots and surrendered his seal; Duke Yu hid on lofty cliffs to nourish his spirit; Liang Sheng went to southern Yue to preserve caution—indeed they could preserve the whole and nourish harmony, level their tracks and suffuse with moisture, spread fragrance through winter, and alone flourish amid snow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zizhou drifted the blue sea and coiled like a dragon; Wu Jihu abruptly renounced imperial power; Duke Yu withdrew to high cliffs to nourish his spirit; Liang Sheng went south to Yue and kept himself whole. All of them preserved their true selves, lived in quiet obscurity, sent forth fragrance in winter, and flourished alone through snow.

manualTranslations.zh: 「今少子睎冥風，弱挺秀容，奇以幼齡，翰披孺童。
manualTranslations.literal: "Now you, young sir, gaze toward the dark wind, in youth already upright and of fine countenance, extraordinary from tender years, your brush surpassing mere boys."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Yet you, young sir, aspire to the reclusive way even in youth—handsome of bearing, precocious in talent, your writing already outshining other lads."

manualTranslations.zh: 吐辭則藻落楊班，抗心則志擬高鴻，味道則理貫莊肆，研妙則穎奪豪鋒。
manualTranslations.literal: When you speak, ornament falls before Yang and Ban; when you brace your heart, ambition rivals the high wild goose; when you savor the Way, principle runs through Zhuangzi; when you probe subtlety, keenness seizes the bold edge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your words outshine Yang Xiong and Ban Gu; your spirit aspires as high as wild geese in flight; your grasp of the Way matches Zhuangzi; your subtle insight rivals the sharpest masters.

manualTranslations.zh: 固以騰廣莫而萋蒨，排素薄而青蔥者矣，何必以刑禮為己任，申韓為宏通！
manualTranslations.literal: Already you soar through the vast void in lush splendor, thrusting aside plain thinness for verdant richness—why must punishments and ritual be your charge, Shen and Han your broad mastery!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You already rise through boundless space in full brilliance, casting off the pale and thin for rich green life—why burden yourself with penal law and ritual, or take Shen Buhai and Han Fei as your grand achievement!

manualTranslations.zh: 既登東觀，染史筆；
manualTranslations.literal: You have already ascended the Eastern Pavilion and stained the historian's brush;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have entered the Eastern Pavilion and taken up the historian's brush;

manualTranslations.zh: 又據太學，理儒功。
manualTranslations.literal: again you occupy the Imperial Academy and order Ruist achievement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and you hold post at the Imperial Academy, managing Confucian scholarship.

manualTranslations.zh: 曾無玄韻淡泊，逸氣虛洞，養采幽翳，晦明蒙籠。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet never the dark resonance of quiet detachment, the drifting breath of empty depth, nurturing luster in hidden shade, mingling dark and bright in misted obscurity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet you show none of the dark serenity of detachment, the free breath of empty depth, the cultivation of grace in hidden shade, the mingling of light and shadow in misted obscurity.

manualTranslations.zh: 不追林棲之跡，不希抱鱗之龍，不營練真之術，不慕內聽之聰。
manualTranslations.literal: You do not pursue the tracks of forest dwelling, do not hope for the dragon embracing scales, do not practice the arts of refining truth, do not admire the inner hearing of keen perception.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You do not follow the path of forest reclusion, do not seek the hidden dragon, do not cultivate arts of refining the true self, do not cherish the inner clarity of deep listening.

manualTranslations.zh: 而處泛位以核物，扇塵教以自濛，負鹽車以顯能，飾一己以求恭。
manualTranslations.literal: Instead you occupy a floating post to examine things, fan dusty teaching to cloud yourself, bear the salt cart to display ability, adorn your single self to seek respectability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Instead you hold an empty office to judge affairs, stir dusty doctrine to blind yourself, bear the salt-laden cart to show off talent, and polish your private self to win approval.

manualTranslations.zh: 退不居漆園之場，出不躡曾城之沖，遊不踐綽約之室，諆不希騄駬之蹤；
manualTranslations.literal: In retirement you do not dwell in Zhuangzi's domain, going out you do not tread Zengcheng's heights, in wandering you do not enter rooms of graceful restraint, in planning you do not hope for traces of fine steeds;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In retreat you do not dwell in Zhuangzi's realm; abroad you do not climb immortal heights; in leisure you do not enter chambers of pure refinement; in ambition you do not seek the tracks of noble steeds;

manualTranslations.zh: 徒以區區之懷而整名目之典，覆蕢之量而塞北川之洪，檢名實於俄頃之間，定得失乎一管之鋒。
manualTranslations.literal: you merely use a petty heart to arrange the canons of names and categories, a basket-cover's measure to block the northern river's flood, inspect name and reality in a fleeting moment, and fix gain and loss at the tip of a single brush.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: you merely apply a narrow mind to codify names and categories, a cup's measure to dam a northern flood, judge name and reality in an instant, and settle right and wrong at the point of a single brush.

manualTranslations.zh: 「子若謂我果是邪？
manualTranslations.literal: "If you say I am truly right,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "If you hold that I am truly in the right,

manualTranslations.zh: 則是不必以合俗。
manualTranslations.literal: then one need not conform to custom.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: then there is no need to conform to custom.

manualTranslations.zh: 子若云俗果非邪？
manualTranslations.literal: If you say custom is truly wrong,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you say custom is truly wrong,

manualTranslations.zh: 則俗非不可以苟從。
manualTranslations.literal: then custom is not something one cannot casually follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: then custom is not something one may never follow at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 俗我紛以交爭，利害渾而彌重，何異執朽轡以禦逸駟，承勁風以握秋蓬，役恬性以充勞府，對群物以耦怨雙者乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Custom and I tangle in mutual strife; gain and harm merge and grow heavier—how is this different from grasping rotten reins to rein in galloping teams, facing strong wind while clutching autumn tumbleweed, pressing tranquil nature to fill the laboring heart, and facing all things as paired resentment doubled?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Custom and self clash in endless dispute; profit and harm blur together and weigh ever heavier—what is this but holding rotten reins against a runaway team, gripping autumn tumbleweed in a gale, forcing a tranquil nature into ceaseless toil, and meeting the world only as doubled resentment?

manualTranslations.zh: 子不聞乎終軍之穎，賈生之才，拔奇山東，玉映漢台，可謂響播六合，聲駭嬰孩，而見毀絳灌之口，身離狼狽之災。
manualTranslations.literal: Have you not heard of Zhong Jun's keenness and Jia Yi's talent—raised as marvel east of the mountains, jade reflecting on the Han terrace, one might say their fame resounded through the six directions and their voices startled infants—yet they were slandered by the mouths of Zhou Bo and Guan Ying and personally met the disaster of disgrace?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Have you not heard of Zhong Jun's brilliance and Jia Yi's genius—outstanding talents of Shandong, jade gleaming at the Han court, their fame echoing through the realm and their names startling even children—yet destroyed by the tongues of Zhou Bo and Guan Ying and brought to ruin and disgrace?

manualTranslations.zh: 由此言之，名為實賓，福萌禍胎，朝敷榮華，夕歸塵埃，未若澄虛心于玄圃，廕瑤林于蓬萊，絕世事而雋黃綺，鼓滄川而浪龍鰓者矣。
manualTranslations.literal: From this it is said: fame is the guest of reality; fortune sprouts the embryo of disaster; morning spreads glory and splendor, evening returns to dust—better to clarify the empty heart in the dark garden, shelter in jade groves at Penglai, cut off worldly affairs and join Huang and Qi in excellence, and drum the blue river into waves for dragon gills.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this we see: fame is but the shadow of substance; fortune breeds disaster; glory at dawn turns to dust by dusk. Far better to clear the heart in the mystic garden, rest beneath jade trees on Penglai, leave the world behind like Huang and Qi, and let the blue river surge for the dragon's gills.

manualTranslations.zh: 蒙竊惑焉。」
manualTranslations.literal: I am privately puzzled by this."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what puzzles me."

manualTranslations.zh: 主人煥耳而笑，欣然而言曰：「夫兩儀既辟，陰陽汗浩，五才迭用，化生紛擾，萬類云云，孰測其兆！
manualTranslations.literal: The host, ears brightening, laughed and spoke with pleasure, saying, "When the two principles were already opened, yin and yang flowed vast, the five talents rotated in use, birth and transformation churned in turmoil, the myriad kinds teemed on—who could fathom their signs!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The host laughed with bright delight, then spoke with pleasure: "Once heaven and earth were formed, yin and yang poured forth in vast motion; the five elements succeeded one another; life churned in endless change; the myriad creatures multiplied—who could read their omens!

manualTranslations.zh: 故不登閬風，安以瞻殊目之形？
manualTranslations.literal: Thus if one does not ascend Langfeng, how may one behold forms of strange eyes?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without climbing Mount Langfeng, how can one behold forms beyond ordinary sight?

manualTranslations.zh: 不步景宿，何以觀恢廓之表？
manualTranslations.literal: If one does not tread Jingsu, how may one view the broad expanse's surface?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without walking among the constellations, how can one see the vast reaches of the cosmos?

manualTranslations.zh: 是以迷粗者循一往之智，狷介者守一方之矯，豈知火林之蔚炎柯，冰津之擢陽草！
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the crude in confusion follow a single course of wisdom; the narrow and rigid guard one corner's perversity—how could they know the fire forest's lush blazing branches, or ice ford's sprouting yang grass!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The coarse in spirit cling to one fixed wisdom; the rigid guard one narrow orthodoxy—how could they know the blazing branches of the fire forest, or yang grass springing from an icy ford!

manualTranslations.zh: 故大人達觀，任化昏曉，出不極勞，處不巢皓，在儒亦儒，在道亦道，運屈則紆其清暉，時申則散其龍藻，此蓋員動之用舍，非尋常之所寶也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the great man sees broadly, entrusting himself to transformation through dusk and dawn; going out he does not exhaust labor, dwelling he does not nest like the white-haired recluse; in Ruism he is Ruist, in the Way he is of the Way; when fortune bends he coils his clear radiance, when the time extends he spreads his dragon ornament—this is the use and release of rounded movement, not what the ordinary prize.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The great man sees far and yields to transformation through night and day; active, he does not exhaust himself; at rest, he does not burrow away like a hermit. Among scholars he is a scholar; among Daoists he is a Daoist. When fortune falters he gathers his clear light; when the time opens he spreads his dragon brilliance. This is the flexible use and release of the rounded way—not the treasure of ordinary men.

manualTranslations.zh: 「今三明互照，二氣載宣，玄教夕凝，朗風晨鮮，道以才暢，化隨理全。
manualTranslations.literal: "Now the three illuminations shine upon one another, the two breaths bear and proclaim; dark teaching congeals at evening, clear wind is fresh at dawn; the Way flows through talent, transformation follows principle to completion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Now the three lights shine together; yin and yang bear full sway; sacred teaching settles at dusk and clear winds freshen at dawn; the Way advances through talent, and transformation completes through principle.

manualTranslations.zh: 故五典克明於百揆，虞音齊響於五弦，安期解褐于秀林，漁父擺鉤于長川。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the Five Canons are clearly achieved among the hundred duties; Yao's music harmonizes on the five strings; Anqi doffs coarse cloth in the elegant grove; the fisherman casts aside his hook on the long river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the Five Canons govern all affairs; Yao's music sounds on the five strings; Anqi lays aside common dress in a fair grove; the fisherman casts off his hook on the long river.

manualTranslations.zh: 如斯則化無不融，道無不延，風澄於俗，波清於川。
manualTranslations.literal: Like this, then transformation has nothing it does not blend, the Way has nothing it does not extend; wind clears over custom, waves clarify upon the stream.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When it is so, transformation leaves nothing unblended and the Way reaches everywhere; winds clear over custom and waves grow calm upon the stream.

manualTranslations.zh: 方將舞黃虯于慶雲，招儀鳳於靈山，流玉醴乎華闥，秀硃草於庭前。
manualTranslations.literal: About to dance with yellow hornless dragons amid auspicious clouds, summon the ceremonial phoenix on the spirit mountain, pour jade nectar in the splendid gate, and show vermillion grass flourishing before the courtyard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yellow hornless dragons will dance in auspicious clouds; the ceremonial phoenix will be summoned on the sacred mountain; jade nectar will flow through splendid halls; vermillion grass will flourish before the courtyard.

manualTranslations.zh: 何有違理之患，累真之嫌！
manualTranslations.literal: What worry of violating principle, what taint of burdening truth!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What fear then of violating principle, or of staining the true self!

manualTranslations.zh: 子徒知辯其說而未測其源，明朝菌不可逾晦朔，蟪蛄無以觀大年，固非管翰之所述，聊敬對以終篇。
manualTranslations.literal: You merely know to debate the argument yet have not fathomed its source; the morning mushroom cannot cross from new moon to full moon, the summer cicada has no means to behold the great year—this is truly not what brush and pipe would record; I respectfully reply only to close the piece.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You know how to argue the words but have not traced their source. A morning mushroom cannot span from new moon to full; a summer cicada cannot know the great year. This is no matter for petty chroniclers to record—I offer this respectful reply only to close the piece.

context.beforeSource: 其文筆數十篇行於世。
context.afterSource: 庾闡，字仲初，潁川鄢陵人也。

context.afterLocal: 庾闡，字仲初，潁川鄢陵人也。

sourceRange.text: 仕郡文學掾，鬱鬱不得志，乃作《釋時論》，其辭曰：東野丈人觀時以居，隱耕汙腴之墟。有冰氏之子者，出自冱寒之谷，過而問塗。丈人曰：「子奚自？」曰：「自涸陰之鄉。」「奚適？」曰：「欲適煌煌之堂。」丈人曰：「入煌煌之堂者，必有赫赫之光。今子困於寒而欲求諸熱，無得熱之方。」冰子瞿然曰：「胡為其然也？」丈人曰：「融融者皆趣熱之士，其得爐冶之門者，惟挾炭之子。苟非斯人，不如其已。」冰子曰：「吾聞宗廟之器不要華林之木，四門之賓何必冠蓋之族。前賢有解韋索而佩硃韍舍徒擔而乘丹轂。由此言之，何恤而無祿！惟先生告我塗之速也。」丈人曰：「嗚呼！子聞得之若是，不知時之在彼。吾將釋子。夫道有安危，時有險易，才有所應，行有所適。英奇奮於從橫之世，賢智顯于霸王之初，當厄難則騁權譎以良圖，值製作則展儒道以暢攄，是則袞龍出於縕褐，卿相起於匹夫，故有朝賤而夕貴，先卷而後舒。當斯時也，豈計門資之高卑，論勢位之輕重乎！今則不然。上聖下明，時隆道寧，群後逸豫，宴安守平。百辟君子，奕世相生，公門有公，卿門有卿。指禿腐骨，不簡蚩儜。多士豐于貴族，爵命不出閨庭。四門穆穆，綺襦是盈，仍叔之子，皆為老成。賤有常辱，貴有常榮，肉食繼踵于華屋，疏飯襲跡於耨耕。談名位者以諂媚附勢，舉高譽者因資而隨形。至乃空囂者以泓噌為雅量，瑣慧者以淺利為槍槍，脢胎者以無檢為弘曠，僂垢者以守意為堅貞。嘲哮者以粗發為高亮，韞蠢者以色厚為篤誠，痷婪者以博納為通濟，眂々者以難入為凝清，拉答者有沈重之譽，嗛閃者得清剿之聲，嗆啍怯畏于謙讓，闒茸勇敢於饕諍。斯皆寒素之死病，榮達之嘉名。凡茲流也，視其用心，察其所安，責人必急，於己恆寬。德無厚而自貴，位未高而自尊，眼罔向而遠視，鼻𪖷𪖐而刺天。忌惡君子，悅媚小人，敖蔑道素，懾籲權門。心以利傾，智以勢惛，姻黨相扇，毀譽交紛。當局迷於所受，聽采惑于所聞。京邑翼翼，群士千億，奔集勢門，求官買職，童僕窺其車乘，閽寺相其服飾，親客陰參於靖室，疏賓徙倚於門側。時因接見，矜曆容色，心懷內荏，外詐剛直，譚道義謂之俗生，論政刑以為鄙極。高會曲宴，惟言遷除消息，官無大小，問是誰力。今以子孤寒，懷真抱素，志陵雲霄，偶景獨步，直順常道，關津難渡，欲騁韓盧，時無狡兔，眾塗圮塞，投足何錯！」於是冰子釋然乃悟曰：「富貴人之所欲，貧賤人之所惡。僕少長於孔顏之門，久處於清寒之路，不謂熱勢自共遮錮。敬承明誨，服我初素，彈琴詠典，以保年祚。伯成、延陵，高節可慕。丹轂滅族，呂霍哀吟，朝榮夕滅，旦飛暮沈。聃周道師，巢由德林。豐屋蔀家，《易》著明箴。人薄位尊，積罰難任，三郤屍晉，宋華咎深，投扃正幅，實獲我心。

manualTranslations.zh: 仕郡文學掾，鬱鬱不得志，乃作《釋時論》，其辭曰：東野丈人觀時以居，隱耕汙腴之墟。
manualTranslations.literal: He served as commandery Instructor Clerk, depressed without realizing his aims—thereupon he composed "Discourse on Discerning the Times," its words saying: East-field Elder observed the age to dwell, hiding himself to plow fertile muddy fields.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He held the minor post of commandery literary instructor, bitter and thwarted, and wrote "Discourse on Discerning the Times," which begins: East-field Elder watched the times and made his home, living in hidden tillage on rich muddy ground.

manualTranslations.zh: 有冰氏之子者，出自冱寒之谷，過而問塗。
manualTranslations.literal: There was a son of the Ice clan who came forth from a valley of freezing cold, passed by and asked the way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A youth of the Ice clan came from a valley of bitter cold and, passing by, asked directions.

manualTranslations.zh: 丈人曰：「子奚自？」
manualTranslations.literal: The elder said, "From where do you come?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The elder asked, "Where do you come from?"

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：「自涸陰之鄉。」
manualTranslations.literal: He said, "From the land of dried shade."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered, "From the land of frozen shade."

manualTranslations.zh: 「奚適？」
manualTranslations.literal: "Where are you going?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "And where are you bound?"

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：「欲適煌煌之堂。」
manualTranslations.literal: He said, "I wish to go to the resplendent hall."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He said, "I wish to reach the resplendent hall."

manualTranslations.zh: 丈人曰：「入煌煌之堂者，必有赫赫之光。
manualTranslations.literal: The elder said, "Those who enter the resplendent hall must have blazing brilliant light.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The elder said, "Those who enter the resplendent hall must carry blazing brilliance.

manualTranslations.zh: 今子困於寒而欲求諸熱，無得熱之方。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now you are trapped in cold yet seek heat from without—you have no means to obtain heat."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You are trapped in cold yet seek warmth from without—you have no way to gain it."

manualTranslations.zh: 冰子瞿然曰：「胡為其然也？」
manualTranslations.literal: Ice-son started and said, "Why is it so?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ice-son started in alarm and asked, "Why should that be so?"

manualTranslations.zh: 丈人曰：「融融者皆趣熱之士，其得爐冶之門者，惟挾炭之子。
manualTranslations.literal: The elder said, "Those who glow warm are all men hurrying toward heat; those who gain entry to the furnace and forge are only sons who carry charcoal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The elder said, "Those who bask in warmth are all men rushing toward heat; only those who carry charcoal may pass through the furnace gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟非斯人，不如其已。」
manualTranslations.literal: If one is not such a man, better to stop."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you are not such a man, you had better turn back."

manualTranslations.zh: 冰子曰：「吾聞宗廟之器不要華林之木，四門之賓何必冠蓋之族。
manualTranslations.literal: Ice-son said, "I have heard that vessels of the ancestral temple need not be of ornamental-forest wood; guests at the four gates need not be of cap-and-canopy clans.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ice-son said, "I have heard that temple vessels need not come from ornamental groves, and guests at the four gates need not be of noble houses.

manualTranslations.zh: 前賢有解韋索而佩硃韍舍徒擔而乘丹轂。
manualTranslations.literal: Former worthies there were who loosed hemp cords and wore vermillion knee-guards, cast aside the porter's pole and rode vermillion carriages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Worthies of old cast off hemp ropes to wear vermillion knee-guards, abandoned the porter's pole to ride vermillion carriages.

manualTranslations.zh: 由此言之，何恤而無祿！
manualTranslations.literal: From this it is said—why worry that there will be no salary!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If that is so, why fear that office and salary will not come!

manualTranslations.zh: 惟先生告我塗之速也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Only, sir, tell me the swift road."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only tell me, sir, the quickest road."

manualTranslations.zh: 丈人曰：「嗚呼！
manualTranslations.literal: The elder said, "Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The elder cried, "Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 子聞得之若是，不知時之在彼。
manualTranslations.literal: You have heard attainment like this, yet do not know that the age lies over there.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have heard that success can come this way, but you do not see that the times have changed.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾將釋子。
manualTranslations.literal: I will explain to you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let me explain it to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫道有安危，時有險易，才有所應，行有所適。
manualTranslations.literal: The Way has safety and danger; the age has hardship and ease; talent has what it answers to; conduct has what it suits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Way has its safe and perilous courses; the times have their hard and easy seasons; talent meets what it is fitted for; action suits what the moment requires.

manualTranslations.zh: 英奇奮於從橫之世，賢智顯于霸王之初，當厄難則騁權譎以良圖，值製作則展儒道以暢攄，是則袞龍出於縕褐，卿相起於匹夫，故有朝賤而夕貴，先卷而後舒。
manualTranslations.literal: Heroes and marvels exerted themselves in the age of vertical and horizontal alliances; worthies and sages showed themselves at the beginning of hegemons and kings; meeting hardship they unleashed stratagem for good plans; meeting creation they spread Ruist Way to pour forth freely—thus dragon robes came from coarse hemp, ministers and chancellors rose from common men; hence morning low and evening noble, first rolled up then unrolled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heroes flourished in the age of warring alliances; worthies shone at the rise of hegemons and kings. In hardship they deployed stratagem; in eras of creation they unfolded Confucian teaching. Dragon robes emerged from coarse cloth; ministers rose from common men. Men were low at dawn and noble by evening; fortune first curled tight, then opened wide.

manualTranslations.zh: 當斯時也，豈計門資之高卑，論勢位之輕重乎！
manualTranslations.literal: In such a time, who would reckon the high or low of family standing, or debate the light or heavy of power and rank!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In such times, who weighed family pedigree or debated the heft of rank and power!

manualTranslations.zh: 今則不然。
manualTranslations.literal: Now it is not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now it is otherwise.

manualTranslations.zh: 上聖下明，時隆道寧，群後逸豫，宴安守平。
manualTranslations.literal: Above, the sage; below, the enlightened; the age lofty, the Way tranquil; the host of lords at ease, feasting in peace and guarding stability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sovereign above is sage; ministers below are enlightened; the age is prosperous and the Way at peace; lords live at ease, feasting in security and guarding stability.

manualTranslations.zh: 百辟君子，奕世相生，公門有公，卿門有卿。
manualTranslations.literal: The hundred ministers and gentlemen beget one another generation after generation; the duke's gate has dukes, the minister's gate has ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: High ministers beget high ministers generation after generation; duke's houses produce dukes, minister's houses produce ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 指禿腐骨，不簡蚩儜。
manualTranslations.literal: Pointing at bald rotten bones, they do not select the ignorant and clumsy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They point to withered bones and never choose the ignorant and crude.

manualTranslations.zh: 多士豐于貴族，爵命不出閨庭。
manualTranslations.literal: Many scholars abound among noble clans; titles and commands do not leave the inner court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Talented men cluster among noble houses; offices and honors never leave the inner court.

manualTranslations.zh: 四門穆穆，綺襦是盈，仍叔之子，皆為老成。
manualTranslations.literal: The four gates are solemn; silk jackets fill them; sons of Chief of Music are all called seasoned elders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The four gates stand solemn; brocade coats fill them; sons of hereditary musicians pass for seasoned elders.

manualTranslations.zh: 賤有常辱，貴有常榮，肉食繼踵于華屋，疏飯襲跡於耨耕。
manualTranslations.literal: The lowly have constant disgrace; the noble have constant glory; meat-eaters follow in succession in splendid houses, plain rice follows in traces upon harrowed fields.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lowly suffer constant shame; the noble enjoy constant honor. Meat-eaters crowd splendid houses in endless succession; plain rice trails behind the plow.

manualTranslations.zh: 談名位者以諂媚附勢，舉高譽者因資而隨形。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who speak of fame and rank use flattery to cling to power; those who raise lofty praise follow resources and shift with form.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men who talk of rank flatter and cling to power; men who win high praise shape themselves to their patrons' resources.

manualTranslations.zh: 至乃空囂者以泓噌為雅量，瑣慧者以淺利為槍槍，脢胎者以無檢為弘曠，僂垢者以守意為堅貞。
manualTranslations.literal: So much so that empty boasters take deep resonance as elegant breadth; petty clever ones take shallow profit as sharpness; timid ones in the womb take lack of restraint as vast openness; hunchbacked filth takes guarding one's intent as steadfast constancy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empty boasters take bombast for breadth of spirit; petty clever men take small gain for sharp wit; the timid take license for magnanimity; the squalid take stubbornness for constancy.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘲哮者以粗發為高亮，韞蠢者以色厚為篤誠，痷婪者以博納為通濟，眂々者以難入為凝清，拉答者有沈重之譽，嗛閃者得清剿之聲，嗆啍怯畏于謙讓，闒茸勇敢於饕諍。
manualTranslations.literal: Mock-shouters take coarse outburst as high brilliance; hidden stupidity takes thick coloration as deep sincerity; gluttonous greed takes broad acceptance as universal passage; squinting eyes take difficulty of entry as austere clarity; fumblers gain reputation for weightiness; modest flashers gain voice for clear cutting; choking stammerers appear timid in humility and yielding; shabby muddle appears brave in greedy quarrel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mockers take coarse shouting for noble brilliance; concealed fools take thick flattery for deep sincerity; gluttons take broad indulgence for worldly mastery; squinting men take aloofness for austere purity; fumblers win praise for gravity; false modesty wins renown for sharp clarity; stammering cowards pass for humility; shabby mediocrities pass for bold disputants.

manualTranslations.zh: 斯皆寒素之死病，榮達之嘉名。
manualTranslations.literal: These are all fatal illnesses of the humble and plain, and fine names of glory and advancement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These are the mortal sickness of poor scholars—and the honored names of worldly success.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡茲流也，視其用心，察其所安，責人必急，於己恆寬。
manualTranslations.literal: All such types, viewing their use of heart and inspecting where they rest—demanding of others they are always harsh; toward themselves always lenient.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All such men, judged by their motives and their comforts, are harsh toward others and lenient toward themselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 德無厚而自貴，位未高而自尊，眼罔向而遠視，鼻𪖷𪖐而刺天。
manualTranslations.literal: Virtue not thick yet they prize themselves; rank not yet high yet they esteem themselves; eyes not turned yet gaze far; noses snorting upward pierce the sky.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without deep virtue they hold themselves dear; without high rank they esteem themselves high; their eyes stare into the distance without looking straight; their nostrils flare toward heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 忌惡君子，悅媚小人，敖蔑道素，懾籲權門。
manualTranslations.literal: They hate and loathe gentlemen, delight in flattering petty men, disdain the plain Way, and cower and plead at power's gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They hate true gentlemen and delight in flattering petty men; they scorn plain integrity and cringe before the gates of power.

manualTranslations.zh: 心以利傾，智以勢惛，姻黨相扇，毀譽交紛。
manualTranslations.literal: Hearts tilt by profit; wisdom dims by power; marriage cliques fan one another; slander and praise tangle together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearts bend to profit; minds grow dull before power; kin and faction stir one another; slander and praise swirl together.

manualTranslations.zh: 當局迷於所受，聽采惑于所聞。
manualTranslations.literal: Those in office are confused by what they receive; in listening and gathering they are deluded by what they hear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men in office are blinded by what they receive; in judgment they are misled by what they hear.

manualTranslations.zh: 京邑翼翼，群士千億，奔集勢門，求官買職，童僕窺其車乘，閽寺相其服飾，親客陰參於靖室，疏賓徙倚於門側。
manualTranslations.literal: The capital stands in array; gentlemen by the billions; they rush and gather at power's gates, seeking office and buying posts; boy servants peer at their carriages and teams; gatekeepers inspect their dress and ornaments; intimate guests secretly wait in quiet rooms; distant guests linger leaning at the gate side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The capital teems with arrayed splendor; thousands upon thousands of scholars rush to powerful gates, seeking office and buying posts. Servants study their carriages; gatekeepers appraise their dress; favored guests wait in private rooms; humble visitors linger at the gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 時因接見，矜曆容色，心懷內荏，外詐剛直，譚道義謂之俗生，論政刑以為鄙極。
manualTranslations.literal: Occasionally received in audience, they display proud bearing and color; hearts hold inner weakness, outwardly feigning uprightness; speaking of the Way and righteousness they call it vulgar living; discussing government and punishment they deem it the depth of baseness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When occasionally received in audience they put on proud looks, weak within yet feigning stern integrity; they call talk of the Way and righteousness vulgar, and treat discussion of government and law as the depth of baseness.

manualTranslations.zh: 高會曲宴，惟言遷除消息，官無大小，問是誰力。
manualTranslations.literal: At lofty gatherings and private banquets they speak only of promotion and removal news; office great or small—they ask whose power it was.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At grand feasts and private banquets they speak only of promotions and dismissals; for every office, high or low, they ask whose influence secured it.

manualTranslations.zh: 今以子孤寒，懷真抱素，志陵雲霄，偶景獨步，直順常道，關津難渡，欲騁韓盧，時無狡兔，眾塗圮塞，投足何錯！」
manualTranslations.literal: Now because you are solitary and cold, embracing truth and holding plainness, ambition vaulting the clouds, walking alone with your shadow, going straight along the common Way—passes and fords are hard to cross; you wish to unleash Han Lu, yet the time has no cunning hare; the many roads are ruined and blocked—where can you set foot without error!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You are solitary and poor, holding truth and plain integrity; your ambition towers to the clouds, yet you walk alone with your shadow, keeping to the straight path. The passes are hard to cross. You would unleash a swift hound, but there is no cunning hare; every road is blocked—where can you set foot without stumbling!"

manualTranslations.zh: 於是冰子釋然乃悟曰：「富貴人之所欲，貧賤人之所惡。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Ice-son, released and enlightened, said, "Wealth and honor are what people desire; poverty and baseness are what people hate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then Ice-son, suddenly enlightened, said, "Wealth and honor are what men desire; poverty and low estate are what men hate.

manualTranslations.zh: 僕少長於孔顏之門，久處於清寒之路，不謂熱勢自共遮錮。
manualTranslations.literal: I from youth grew up at the gate of Confucius and Yan, long dwelt on the road of pure cold—I did not suppose that hot power would together block and bind me.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I was raised from youth in the school of Confucius and Yan Hui and have long walked the road of clean poverty—I never thought the heat of power would shut me in.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬承明誨，服我初素，彈琴詠典，以保年祚。
manualTranslations.literal: Respectfully I receive your clear instruction, return to my original plainness, pluck the zither and chant the classics, to preserve my years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully accept your teaching, return to my original plainness, play the zither and chant the classics, and so preserve my years.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯成、延陵，高節可慕。
manualTranslations.literal: Bo Cheng and Yanling—lofty integrity worthy of admiration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bo Cheng and Ji Zha of Yanling—lofty integrity worthy of admiration.

manualTranslations.zh: 丹轂滅族，呂霍哀吟，朝榮夕滅，旦飛暮沈。
manualTranslations.literal: Vermillion carriages destroy clans; Lü and Huo mourn in lament; morning glory, evening extinction; dawn flying, dusk sinking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Vermillion carriages bring clan destruction; the houses of Lü and Huo ended in lament; glory at dawn dies by dusk; flight at morning sinks by evening.

manualTranslations.zh: 聃周道師，巢由德林。
manualTranslations.literal: Laozi and Zhuangzi were teachers of the Way; Chao Fu and Xu You were groves of virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Laozi and Zhuangzi were masters of the Way; Chao Fu and Xu You were forests of virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐屋蔀家，《易》著明箴。
manualTranslations.literal: A grand house shadows the family—the "Changes" sets forth a clear admonition.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A grand house casts shadow over the family—the "Book of Changes" gives clear warning.

manualTranslations.zh: 人薄位尊，積罰難任，三郤屍晉，宋華咎深，投扃正幅，實獲我心。
manualTranslations.literal: Men slight yet rank honored; accumulated punishment hard to bear; the Three Xi left corpses in Jin; Song Hua's blame was deep—casting the bolt and straightening the hem truly obtained my heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When worth is slight yet rank is high, accumulated guilt becomes unbearable; the Three Xi families left corpses in Jin; Song Hua's fault ran deep. To bolt the door and straighten one's robe—that truly wins my heart.

context.afterSource: 羅含，字君章，桂陽耒陽人也。

sourceRange.text: 其辭曰：悠悠太上，人之厥初。皇極肇建，彝倫攸敷。五德更運，應錄受符。陶唐既謝，天曆在虞。于時上帝，乃顧惟眷。光我晉祚，應期納禪。位以龍飛，文以豹變。玄澤滂流，仁風潛扇。區內宅心，方隅回面。天垂其象，地耀其文。鳳鳴朝陽，龍翔景雲。嘉禾重穎，蓂莢載芬。率土咸寧，人胥悅欣。恢恢皇度，穆穆聖容。言思其允，貌思其恭。在視斯明。在聽斯聰。登庸以德，明試以功。其恭惟何？昧旦丕顯。無義不經，無理不踐。行舍其華，言去其辯。遊心至虛，同規易簡。六府孔修，九有來踐。澤罔不被，化莫不加。聲教南暨，西漸流沙。幽人肆險，遠國忘遐；越常重譯，充牣皇家。峨峨列辟，赫赫武臣。內和五品，外威四賓。順時貢職，入覲天人。備言錫命，羽蓋硃輪。貽宴好會，不常厥數。神心所授，不言而喻。于時肆射，弓矢斯具。發彼互的，有酒斯飫。文武之道，厥猷未墜。在昔先王，射御茲器。示武懼荒，過則有失。凡厥羣后，無懈於位。

context.beforeSource: 帝于華林園宴射，貞賦詩最美。
context.afterSource: 初置太子中庶子官，貞與護軍長史孔恂俱為之。

manualTranslations.zh: 其辭曰：悠悠太上，人之厥初。
manualTranslations.literal: Its words said: far, far back in highest antiquity was man's primal origin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The poem begins: from remotest antiquity came mankind's earliest beginnings.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇極肇建，彝倫攸敷。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial pole was first established, and the constant norms were thereby spread abroad.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The royal center was first established, and the enduring norms of human conduct were laid out.

manualTranslations.zh: 五德更運，應錄受符。
manualTranslations.literal: The five virtues turned in succession; matching Heaven's register, he received the mandate tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The succession of the Five Virtues turned, and Heaven's register matched as the mandate token was received.

manualTranslations.zh: 陶唐既謝，天曆在虞。
manualTranslations.literal: After Tao Tang had declined, Heaven's calendar rested with Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yao of Tao Tang passed from the stage, Heaven's succession passed to Shun of Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 于時上帝，乃顧惟眷。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the Lord on High then turned His gaze with favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the Lord on High turned His gaze and showed His favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 光我晉祚，應期納禪。
manualTranslations.literal: He brightened our Jin fortune and, responding to the appointed season, received the abdication.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He brightened the house of Jin and, at the appointed time, received the abdication of the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 位以龍飛，文以豹變。
manualTranslations.literal: The throne was taken by dragon-flight, and culture was renewed by leopard-transformation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The throne was taken like a dragon soaring, and culture was renewed like a leopard changing its spots.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄澤滂流，仁風潛扇。
manualTranslations.literal: Dark beneficence poured in torrents, and a benevolent wind secretly fanned abroad.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dark beneficence poured forth in abundance, and a humane breeze quietly stirred.

manualTranslations.zh: 區內宅心，方隅回面。
manualTranslations.literal: Within the realm hearts made their home, and at the four corners faces turned back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All within the realm gave their hearts, and from every quarter faces turned toward the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 天垂其象，地耀其文。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven hung its emblems, and earth shone its patterned brilliance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven displayed its signs, and earth gleamed with its patterned brilliance.

manualTranslations.zh: 鳳鳴朝陽，龍翔景雲。
manualTranslations.literal: The phoenix cried toward the morning sun, and the dragon soared amid glorious clouds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The phoenix sang facing the morning sun, and the dragon soared amid glorious clouds.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉禾重穎，蓂莢載芬。
manualTranslations.literal: Fine grain bore double ears, and lucky pods spread their fragrance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Excellent grain bore double heads, and auspicious pods spread their fragrance.

manualTranslations.zh: 率土咸寧，人胥悅欣。
manualTranslations.literal: All the earth alike was tranquil, and every man was pleased and glad.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All under Heaven was at peace, and every man rejoiced.

manualTranslations.zh: 恢恢皇度，穆穆聖容。
manualTranslations.literal: Vast, vast was the imperial measure, and solemn, solemn the sage countenance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The imperial way was broad and far-reaching, and the sage sovereign's bearing was grave and serene.

manualTranslations.zh: 言思其允，貌思其恭。
manualTranslations.literal: In speech he thought of sincerity, and in appearance he thought of reverence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In speech he sought truthfulness, and in demeanor he sought reverence.

manualTranslations.zh: 在視斯明。
manualTranslations.literal: In what he looked upon, thus he was luminous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In what he saw, he was luminous.

manualTranslations.zh: 在聽斯聰。
manualTranslations.literal: In what he heard, thus he was penetrating.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In what he heard, he was penetrating.

manualTranslations.zh: 登庸以德，明試以功。
manualTranslations.literal: He promoted the worthy by virtue and clearly tested men by merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He promoted men by virtue and clearly tested them by merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 其恭惟何？
manualTranslations.literal: His reverence—what was it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What was the nature of his reverence?

manualTranslations.zh: 昧旦丕顯。
manualTranslations.literal: Before dawn he was greatly manifest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before dawn he was already at work, making his virtue brilliantly plain.

manualTranslations.zh: 無義不經，無理不踐。
manualTranslations.literal: No righteousness went unexpounded, and no right principle went untrodden.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No principle of righteousness went unuttered, and no right path went unfollowed.

manualTranslations.zh: 行舍其華，言去其辯。
manualTranslations.literal: In conduct he set aside ornament, and in speech he put away empty argument.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In conduct he set aside mere ornament, and in speech he put away empty rhetoric.

manualTranslations.zh: 遊心至虛，同規易簡。
manualTranslations.literal: His mind wandered to utmost emptiness, and all followed the same rule of ease and simplicity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His heart rested in utmost emptiness, and all followed the same rule of ease and simplicity.

manualTranslations.zh: 六府孔修，九有來踐。
manualTranslations.literal: The six treasuries were greatly ordered, and the nine domains came to tread his rule.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The six treasuries were fully ordered, and the nine regions all came to follow his rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 澤罔不被，化莫不加。
manualTranslations.literal: His bounty was nowhere unspread, and his transforming influence was nowhere not applied.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His bounty reached everywhere, and his transforming power touched all.

manualTranslations.zh: 聲教南暨，西漸流沙。
manualTranslations.literal: His voice and teaching reached southward and penetrated westward even to the Flowing Sands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Civilizing influence spread to the south and westward even to the Flowing Sands.

manualTranslations.zh: 幽人肆險，遠國忘遐；
manualTranslations.literal: Recluses left their fastnesses, and distant states forgot their remoteness;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recluses abandoned their strongholds, and distant lands forgot how far away they were;

manualTranslations.zh: 越常重譯，充牣皇家。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuechang came with repeated interpreters and filled the imperial house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuechang sent envoys through repeated interpreters, thronging the imperial court.

manualTranslations.zh: 峨峨列辟，赫赫武臣。
manualTranslations.literal: Towering, towering stood the arrayed lords, and blazing, blazing the martial ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The feudal lords stood towering in rank, and martial ministers shone in splendor.

manualTranslations.zh: 內和五品，外威四賓。
manualTranslations.literal: Within he harmonized the five ranks of kin, and without he awed the four frontier peoples.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within he harmonized the five grades of kin, and without he overawed the four frontier peoples.

manualTranslations.zh: 順時貢職，入覲天人。
manualTranslations.literal: Following the seasons they paid tribute and duty and entered to behold Heaven's son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the proper seasons they paid tribute and came to court to behold the Son of Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 備言錫命，羽蓋硃輪。
manualTranslations.literal: Edicts of appointment were fully bestowed, with feathered canopies and vermilion wheels.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Edicts of appointment were lavishly bestowed, with feathered canopies and vermilion wheels marking their honors.

manualTranslations.zh: 貽宴好會，不常厥數。
manualTranslations.literal: He granted banquets and friendly gatherings without fixing their number.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He lavished feasts and cordial gatherings without counting how often.

manualTranslations.zh: 神心所授，不言而喻。
manualTranslations.literal: What the divine mind imparted was understood without words being spoken.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What the divine heart conveyed needed no words to make it understood.

manualTranslations.zh: 于時肆射，弓矢斯具。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time came the shooting display, and bows and arrows were there prepared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then came the archery display, with bows and arrows all ready.

manualTranslations.zh: 發彼互的，有酒斯飫。
manualTranslations.literal: They loosed arrows at those layered targets, and where there was wine there was feasting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They loosed arrows at the layered targets, and wine was there for all to enjoy.

manualTranslations.zh: 文武之道，厥猷未墜。
manualTranslations.literal: The way of civil and martial affairs had not yet fallen from its grand design.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The way of wen and wu had not yet fallen from practice.

manualTranslations.zh: 在昔先王，射御茲器。
manualTranslations.literal: In ancient times the former kings practiced archery and charioteering with these implements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity the former kings practiced archery and charioteering with such gear.

manualTranslations.zh: 示武懼荒，過則有失。
manualTranslations.literal: They displayed martial readiness to fear dissipation, for excess then brought failure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They showed martial readiness to guard against decadence, for excess brings failure.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡厥羣后，無懈於位。
manualTranslations.literal: For all those assembled lords, let there be no slackening in their posts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let all the assembled lords never slacken in their duties.

sourceRange.text: 其辭曰：中興二十三載，余忝守衡南，鼓栧三江，路次巴陵，望君山而過洞庭，涉湘川而觀汨水，臨賈生投書之川，慨以永懷矣。及造長沙，觀其遺象，喟然有感，乃吊之云：偉哉蘭生而芳，玉產而潔，陽葩熙冰，寒松負雪，莫邪挺鍔，天驥汗血，苟云其雋，誰與比傑！是以高明倬茂，獨發奇秀，道率天真，不議世疚，煥乎若望舒耀景而焯群星，矯乎若翔鸞拊翼而逸宇宙也。飛榮洛汭，擢穎山東，質清浮磬，聲若孤桐，琅琅其璞，岩岩其峰，通道居正，而以天下為公，方駕逸步，不以曲路期通。是以張高弘悲，聲激柱落，清唱未和，而桑濮代作，雖有惠音，莫過《韶》《濩》；雖有騰鱗，終僕一壑。嗚呼！大庭既邈，玄風悠緬，皇道不以智隆，上德不以仁顯。三五親譽，其輒可仰而標；霸功雖逸，其塗可翼而闡，悲矣先生，何命之蹇！懷寶如玉，而生運之淺！昔咎繇謨虞，呂尚歸昌，德協充符，乃應帝王。夷吾相桓，漢登蕭張；草廬三顧，臭若蘭芳。是以道隱則蠖屈，數感則鳳睹，若棲不擇木，翔非九五，雖曰玉折，雋才何補！夫心非死灰，智必存形，形托神用，故能全生。奈何蘭膏，揚芳漢庭，摧景飆風，獨喪厥明。悠悠太素，存亡一指，道來斯通，世往斯圮。吾哀其生，未見其死，敢不敬吊，寄之淥水。

context.beforeSource: 頃之，出補零陵太守，入湘川，吊賈誼。
context.afterSource: 後以疾，徵拜給事中，復領著作。

manualTranslations.zh: 其辭曰：中興二十三載，余忝守衡南，鼓栧三江，路次巴陵，望君山而過洞庭，涉湘川而觀汨水，臨賈生投書之川，慨以永懷矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Its words said: in the twenty-third year of the Restoration, I am honored to guard south of Heng, beating oars on the three rivers; on the road I passed Baling, gazed at Jun Mountain and crossed Dongting, forded the Xiang and viewed the Miluo, and stood by the river where Jia Yi cast his letter into the water, stirred to lasting remembrance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The piece begins: in the twenty-third year of the Restoration, while I held office south of Mount Heng and rowed the three rivers, my route took me through Baling; I looked toward Jun Mountain and crossed Lake Dongting, traveled the Xiang and came to the Miluo, and stood by the stream where Jia Yi had cast his letter into the water, filled with enduring sorrow.

manualTranslations.zh: 及造長沙，觀其遺象，喟然有感，乃吊之云：偉哉蘭生而芳，玉產而潔，陽葩熙冰，寒松負雪，莫邪挺鍔，天驥汗血，苟云其雋，誰與比傑！
manualTranslations.literal: When I reached Changsha and beheld his surviving image, I sighed with deep feeling and mourned him, saying: how great—orchid born and fragrant, jade produced and pure; sunny blossoms thrive upon ice, cold pine bears snow; Mo Ye draws its blade, the heavenly steed sweats blood; if one calls such talent outstanding, who could be matched as his peer!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I came to Changsha and saw what remained of him, I sighed with deep emotion and composed this lament: how splendid—the orchid born fragrant, jade mined pure; blossoms warm the ice, the pine shoulders snow; Mo Ye unsheathes its edge, the heavenly courser sweats blood—if such genius is called supreme, who could stand beside him as an equal!

manualTranslations.zh: 是以高明倬茂，獨發奇秀，道率天真，不議世疚，煥乎若望舒耀景而焯群星，矯乎若翔鸞拊翼而逸宇宙也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus lofty and brilliantly abundant, he alone brought forth singular excellence; the Way followed native truth and did not debate worldly afflictions; radiant as Wang Shu shining upon the scene and illuminating the host of stars, soaring as a flying phoenix beating its wings and escaping the cosmos.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus eminent and splendid, he alone unfolded rare brilliance; the Way in him followed innate truth and he did not wrangle over worldly woes; he shone like the moon-charioteer brightening the sky and outshining the stars, and soared like a phoenix beating its wings and fleeing beyond the world.

manualTranslations.zh: 飛榮洛汭，擢穎山東，質清浮磬，聲若孤桐，琅琅其璞，岩岩其峰，通道居正，而以天下為公，方駕逸步，不以曲路期通。
manualTranslations.literal: Glory flew at the bend of the Luo, and distinguished talent rose in Shandong; his substance was clear as a floating stone chime, his voice like a solitary paulownia; lustrous was his uncut jade, towering his peak; he opened the Way and dwelt in rectitude, taking all under Heaven as public, matching lofty paces and not expecting passage by crooked paths.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fame rose at Luoyang, and his brilliance emerged in the east; his character was clear as a resonant stone, his voice like a lone paulownia tree; his jade gleamed uncut, his peak stood sheer; he held the Way in rectitude and treated the realm as common ground, keeping pace with the great and never seeking advancement by devious means.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以張高弘悲，聲激柱落，清唱未和，而桑濮代作，雖有惠音，莫過《韶》《濩》；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus he raised high and spread his grief; his voice was so intense that pillars fell; his clear song had not yet found harmony when licentious music of Sang and Pu took its place; though there was gracious sound, none surpassed the Shao and Hu;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So he lifted his voice in vast sorrow until the sound shook pillars from their bases; his pure song had not yet found harmony when the wanton tunes of Sang and Pu replaced it; though gracious music existed, none surpassed the Shao and Hu;

manualTranslations.zh: 雖有騰鱗，終僕一壑。
manualTranslations.literal: Though there were leaping scales, in the end they served only one gully.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though talent leapt like fish in flood, in the end it was confined to a single ravine.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗚呼！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 大庭既邈，玄風悠緬，皇道不以智隆，上德不以仁顯。
manualTranslations.literal: The age of the Great Hall is already remote, the dark wind far and withdrawn; the imperial Way is not exalted by intelligence alone, and highest virtue is not displayed by benevolence alone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The age of Great Harmony is already distant, and the subtle Way lies far behind; the royal path is not raised by wit alone, nor is supreme virtue shown by kindness alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 三五親譽，其輒可仰而標；
manualTranslations.literal: The intimate praise of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—their tracks can be looked up to and taken as standards;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The close renown of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors offers tracks one may look up to and take as models;

manualTranslations.zh: 霸功雖逸，其塗可翼而闡，悲矣先生，何命之蹇！
manualTranslations.literal: Hegemonic achievements though transcendent—their paths can be winged and expounded; how sad, Master—how obstructed your fate!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though hegemonic merit may be sublime, its path can still be traced and explained; how pitiable, sir—how harsh was your fate!

manualTranslations.zh: 懷寶如玉，而生運之淺！
manualTranslations.literal: He treasured talent like jade, yet life and fortune were shallow!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He bore talent like jade in his breast, yet his life and his times were too brief!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔咎繇謨虞，呂尚歸昌，德協充符，乃應帝王。
manualTranslations.literal: In old times Gao Yao counseled at Yu's court, and Lü Shang returned to Chang; virtue matched the fullness of the mandate and thus answered to emperors and kings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Long ago Gao Yao advised Shun, and Lü Shang came home to the house of Chang; when virtue matched Heaven's fullness, men answered to emperors and kings.

manualTranslations.zh: 夷吾相桓，漢登蕭張；
manualTranslations.literal: Guan Zhong served Duke Huan, and Han elevated Xiao and Zhang;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guan Yiwu served Duke Huan of Qi, and the Han raised Xiao He and Zhang Liang;

manualTranslations.zh: 草廬三顧，臭若蘭芳。
manualTranslations.literal: Three visits were paid to the thatched hut, fragrant as orchid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three visits were made to the thatched cottage, sweet as orchid fragrance.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以道隱則蠖屈，數感則鳳睹，若棲不擇木，翔非九五，雖曰玉折，雋才何補！
manualTranslations.literal: Thus when the Way is hidden the inchworm curls up, and when fate responds the phoenix appears; if one perches without choosing the tree and soars not at the ninth and fifth positions, though it is called jade broken, what use is brilliant talent!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus when the Way lies hidden the inchworm curls, and when the times respond the phoenix appears; if one roosts without choosing the right tree and flies not at the sovereign height, though jade may break, what good is transcendent talent!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫心非死灰，智必存形，形托神用，故能全生。
manualTranslations.literal: The heart is not dead ash, wisdom must preserve form, and form is entrusted to the spirit's function—thus one can preserve life whole.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The heart is not dead ashes, wisdom must keep its form, and form relies on the spirit's use—by this a man may preserve his life entire.

manualTranslations.zh: 奈何蘭膏，揚芳漢庭，摧景飆風，獨喪厥明。
manualTranslations.literal: Alas for orchid ointment spreading fragrance in the Han court—scattered glory in a whirlwind, alone it lost its brilliance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas for orchid balm that spread its fragrance in the Han court, only to have its radiance torn away by a sudden gale and lose its light alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 悠悠太素，存亡一指，道來斯通，世往斯圮。
manualTranslations.literal: Far, far primordial simplicity—existence and extinction in one finger's span; when the Way comes, thus it connects, and when the age passes, thus it collapses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Remote primordial simplicity holds life and death in a single moment; when the Way arrives, all opens, and when the age departs, all falls to ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾哀其生，未見其死，敢不敬吊，寄之淥水。
manualTranslations.literal: I mourn his life and have not seen his death; how dare I not reverently mourn him—I send this to the clear waters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I grieve for his life though I did not witness his death; how could I fail to offer this reverent lament and commit it to the clear stream?

context.beforeSource: 明子有父風，最知名，官至臨賀太守。
context.afterSource: 伏滔，字玄度，平昌安丘人也。

sourceRange.text: 其上篇曰：淮南者，三代揚州之分也。當春秋時，吳、楚、陳、蔡之與地。戰國之末，楚全有之，而考烈王都焉。秦並天下，建立郡縣，是為九江。劉項之際，號曰東楚。爰自戰國至於晉之中興，六百有餘年，保淮南者九姓，稱兵者十一人，皆亡不旋踵，禍溢於世，而終莫戒焉。其天時歟，地勢歟，人事歟？何喪亂之若是也！試商較而論之。夫懸象著明，而休征表於列宿；山河衿帶，而地險彰於丘陵；治亂推移，而興亡見於人事。由此而觀，則兼也必矣。昔妖星出於東南而弱楚以亡，飛孛橫於天漢而劉安誅絕，近則火星晨見而王淩首謀，長彗宵暎而毋丘襲亂。斯則表乎天時也。彼壽陽者，南引荊汝之利，東連三吳之富；北接梁宋，平塗不過七日；西援陳許，水陸不出千里；外有江湖之阻，內保淮肥之固。龍泉之陂，良疇萬頃，舒六之貢，利盡蠻越，金石皮革之具萃焉，苞木箭竹之族生焉，山湖藪澤之隈，水旱之所不害，土產草滋之實，荒年之所取給。此則系乎地利乎也。其俗尚氣力而多勇悍，其人習戰爭而貴詐偽，豪右並兼之門，十室而七；藏甲挾劍之家，比屋而發。然而仁義之化不漸，刑法之令不及，所以屢多亡國也。昔考烈以衰弱之楚屢遷其都，外迫強秦之威，內遘陽申之禍，逃死劫殺，三世而滅。黥布以三雄之選，功成垓下，淮陰既囚，梁越受戮，嫌結震主之威，慮生同體之禍，遂謀圖全之計，庶幾後亡之福，眾潰于一戰，身脂於漢斧。劉長支庶，奄王大國，承喪亂之餘，禦新化之俗，無德而寵，欲極禍發。王安內懷先父之憾，外眩奸臣之說，招引賓客，沈溺數術，藉二世之資，恃戈甲之盛，屈強江淮之上，西向而圖宗國，言未絕口，身嗣俱滅。李憲因亡新之余，袁術當衰漢之末，負力幸亂，遂生僭逆之計，建號九江，稱制下邑，狼狽奔亡，傾城受戮。及至彥雲、仲恭、公休之徒，或憑宿名，或怙前功，握兵淮楚，力制東夏，屬當多難之世，仍值廢興之會，謀非所議，相系禍敗。祖約助逆，身亡家族。彼十亂者，成乎人事者也。然則侵弱昏迷，以至絕滅，亡楚當之。恃強畏逼，遂謀叛亂，黥布有焉。二王遘逆，寵之之過也。公路僭偽，乘釁之盜也。二將以圖功首難，士少以驕矜樂禍。本其所因，考其成跡，皆寵盛禍淫，福過災生，而制之不漸，積之有由也。其下篇曰：昔高祖之誅黥布也，撮三策之要，馳赦過之書，乘人主之威以除逆節之虜，然猶決戰陳都，暴屍橫野，僅乃克之，害亦深矣！長安之謀，雖兵未交于山東，禍未遍於天下，而馳說之士與闔境之人幽囚誅放者，亦已眾矣。光武連兵于肥舒，魏祖馳馬於蘄苦，而廬九之間流溺兵凶者十而七八焉。夫王淩面縛，得之于砎石；仲恭接刃，成之於後覺也。而高祖以之宵征，世宗以之發疾，豈不勤哉！文皇挾萬乘之威，杖伊周之權，內舉京畿之眾，外征四海之銳，雲合雨集，推鋒以臨淮浦，而誕欽晏然，方嬰城自固，憑軾以觀王師。於是築長圍，起棼櫓，高壁連塹，負戈擊柝以守之。自夏及春，而後始知亡焉。然則屠城之禍，其可極言乎？約之出奔，淮左為墟，悲夫！信哉魯哀之言，夫生乎深宮，長於膏梁，憂懼不切於身，榮辱不交於前，則其仁義之本淺矣。奉以南面之尊，藉以列城之富，宅以制險之居，養以眾強之盛，而無德以臨之，無制以節之，則厭溢樂禍之心生矣。夫以昏主禦奸臣，利甲資堅城，偽令行于封內，邪惠結于人心，乘間幸濟之說日交於側，猾詐錮咎之群各馳於前，見利如歸，安在其不為亂乎！況乘舊寵，挾前功，畏逼懼亡，以謀圖身之舉者，望其俯首就羈，不亦迂哉！《易》稱「履霜堅冰，馴致之道，」蓋言漸也。嗚呼！斯所以亂臣賊子亡國覆家累世而不絕者歟！昔先生之宰天下也，選於有德，訪之三吏，正其分位元，明其等級，畫之封疆，宣之政令，上下有序，無僭差之嫌，四人安業，無並兼之國。三載考陟，功罪不得逃其跡，九伐時修，刑賞無所謬其實。令之有漸，軌之有度，寵之有節，權不外授，威不下黷，所以杜其萌際，重其名器，深根固本，傳之百世。雖時有盛衰，弱者無所懼其亡；道有興廢，強者不得資其弊。夫如是，將使天下從風，穆然軌道，慶自一人，惠流萬國，安有向時之患哉！
