manualTranslations.zh: 其上篇曰：淮南者，三代揚州之分也。
manualTranslations.literal: Its upper chapter says: Huainan is the allotment of Yangzhou in the Three Dynasties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The upper essay begins: the Huainan region was the Yangzhou domain of the Three Dynasties.

manualTranslations.zh: 當春秋時，吳、楚、陳、蔡之與地。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn period, it was territory shared with Wu, Chu, Chen, and Cai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Spring and Autumn era it lay among the lands of Wu, Chu, Chen, and Cai.

manualTranslations.zh: 戰國之末，楚全有之，而考烈王都焉。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of the Warring States, Chu wholly possessed it, and King Kaolie made it his capital there.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the close of the Warring States Chu held it entirely, and King Kaolie established his capital there.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦並天下，建立郡縣，是為九江。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin united the realm, established commanderies and counties, and this became Jiujiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Qin unified the empire and instituted the commandery-county system, the area became Jiujiang commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 劉項之際，號曰東楚。
manualTranslations.literal: In the age of Liu and Xiang, it was called Eastern Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the struggle between the Liu and Xiang houses it was known as Eastern Chu.

manualTranslations.zh: 爰自戰國至於晉之中興，六百有餘年，保淮南者九姓，稱兵者十一人，皆亡不旋踵，禍溢於世，而終莫戒焉。
manualTranslations.literal: From the Warring States down to the restoration of Jin, more than six hundred years—nine houses held Huainan, eleven men raised arms; all perished without turning heel, calamity overflowed the age, and in the end none took warning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the Warring States through the Jin restoration, a span of more than six centuries, nine lineages held the Huainan region and eleven men took up arms; every one perished almost at once, disaster spread through the age, and still no one heeded the lesson.

manualTranslations.zh: 其天時歟，地勢歟，人事歟？
manualTranslations.literal: Was it celestial timing, terrain and momentum, or human affairs?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Was the cause celestial timing, geographical advantage, or human conduct?

manualTranslations.zh: 何喪亂之若是也！
manualTranslations.literal: Why was disorder and ruin thus!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why has turmoil been so relentless!

manualTranslations.zh: 試商較而論之。
manualTranslations.literal: Let us compare and weigh the matter and discuss it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let us weigh the evidence and examine the question.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫懸象著明，而休征表於列宿；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's suspended images are made manifest, and auspicious signs appear among the constellations;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven displays its signs clearly, and favorable or ominous portents appear among the stars;

manualTranslations.zh: 山河衿帶，而地險彰於丘陵；
manualTranslations.literal: rivers and mountains form collar and belt, and the land's peril is shown in hills and mounds;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: rivers and mountains gird the land like collar and sash, and strategic danger is revealed in its hills;

manualTranslations.zh: 治亂推移，而興亡見於人事。
manualTranslations.literal: order and disorder shift in turn, and rise and fall are seen in human affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: order and chaos alternate, and the rise and fall of states are disclosed in human affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 由此而觀，則兼也必矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Viewed from this, then all three together is certain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, all three factors must operate together.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔妖星出於東南而弱楚以亡，飛孛橫於天漢而劉安誅絕，近則火星晨見而王淩首謀，長彗宵暎而毋丘襲亂。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly a demon star appeared in the southeast and weak Chu thereby perished; a flying comet stretched across the Heavenly River and Liu An was executed to extinction; recently Mars appeared at dawn and Wang Ling first plotted rebellion; a long comet shone through the night and Guanqiu Jian launched disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity a baleful star rose in the southeast and enfeebled Chu was destroyed; a comet swept across the Milky Way and Liu An was put to death with his house; in recent times Mars appeared at dawn as Wang Ling first conspired, and a long comet blazed by night when Guanqiu Jian rose in revolt.

manualTranslations.zh: 斯則表乎天時也。
manualTranslations.literal: This then is displayed in celestial timing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These are manifestations of Heaven's timing.

manualTranslations.zh: 彼壽陽者，南引荊汝之利，東連三吳之富；
manualTranslations.literal: That Shouyang—southward draws the profit of Jing and Ru; eastward links the wealth of the Three Wu regions;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shouyang draws southern profit from the Jing and Ru corridor and eastern wealth from the Three Wu lands;

manualTranslations.zh: 北接梁宋，平塗不過七日；
manualTranslations.literal: northward adjoins Liang and Song, and level roads require no more than seven days;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: to the north it meets Liang and Song, reachable over level roads in no more than seven days;

manualTranslations.zh: 西援陳許，水陸不出千里；
manualTranslations.literal: westward supports Chen and Xu, and by water or land it is not beyond a thousand li;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: to the west it links Chen and Xu, within a thousand li by river or road;

manualTranslations.zh: 外有江湖之阻，內保淮肥之固。
manualTranslations.literal: outside it has the barrier of rivers and lakes; inside it preserves the solidity of the Huai and Fei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: rivers and lakes guard it without, while the Huai and Fei basins secure it within.

manualTranslations.zh: 龍泉之陂，良疇萬頃，舒六之貢，利盡蠻越，金石皮革之具萃焉，苞木箭竹之族生焉，山湖藪澤之隈，水旱之所不害，土產草滋之實，荒年之所取給。
manualTranslations.literal: The Longquan reservoir, fine fields by the myriad mu; tribute from Shu and Liu, profit extending to the Man and Yue; implements of metal, stone, leather, and hide gather there; clans of wrapped timber and arrow bamboo grow there; recesses of mountains, lakes, marshes, and swamps where flood and drought do not harm; native products and nourishing grasses and fruits, supplies drawn upon in lean years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Longquan reservoir and ten thousand mu of fertile fields; tribute from Shu and Liu channels profit as far as the southern barbarian lands; metal, stone, leather, and harness are gathered there, and timber and arrow bamboo abound; in the sheltered margins of hills, lakes, and marshes drought and flood do little harm, while native grains, herbs, and fruits sustain the people in years of famine.

manualTranslations.zh: 此則系乎地利乎也。
manualTranslations.literal: This then is tied to geographical advantage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This, then, depends on geographical advantage.

manualTranslations.zh: 其俗尚氣力而多勇悍，其人習戰爭而貴詐偽，豪右並兼之門，十室而七；
manualTranslations.literal: Its customs honor physical force and produce many fierce and bold men; its people are practiced in warfare and prize deceit and falsehood; among powerful houses that annex and merge, seven in ten dwellings;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Local custom esteems brute strength and breeds fierce warriors; the people are seasoned in war and prize cunning stratagem; in seven of every ten households powerful families annex their neighbors;

manualTranslations.zh: 藏甲挾劍之家，比屋而發。
manualTranslations.literal: houses that store armor and carry swords rise house by house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: homes that hoard armor and bear swords appear in nearly every dwelling.

manualTranslations.zh: 然而仁義之化不漸，刑法之令不及，所以屢多亡國也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the transforming influence of benevolence and righteousness does not gradually reach them, and the commands of penal law do not extend to them—therefore states here have repeatedly perished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the civilizing force of benevolence and righteousness never takes root, and penal statutes never reach them—hence the repeated ruin of states in this region.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔考烈以衰弱之楚屢遷其都，外迫強秦之威，內遘陽申之禍，逃死劫殺，三世而滅。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Kaolie, with a weakened Chu, repeatedly moved his capital; outwardly pressed by mighty Qin's might, inwardly meeting Lord Yang Shen's calamity; fleeing death and suffering robbery and murder, in three generations it was extinguished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Kaolie of a declining Chu moved his capital again and again, threatened without by Qin's power and torn within by the disaster of Lord Chunshen; amid flight, slaughter, and plunder, his line was extinguished in three generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 黥布以三雄之選，功成垓下，淮陰既囚，梁越受戮，嫌結震主之威，慮生同體之禍，遂謀圖全之計，庶幾後亡之福，眾潰于一戰，身脂於漢斧。
manualTranslations.literal: Ying Bu, chosen among the three heroes, achieved merit at Gaixia; once Huaiyin was imprisoned and Liang and Yue were executed, suspicion formed over the awe of a ruler who trembled before his subjects, fear arose of the calamity of shared flesh and blood; then he plotted a plan to preserve himself whole, hoping perhaps for the fortune of dying later—his host collapsed in one battle, and his body greased the Han axe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ying Bu, one of the three great champions, had won glory at Gaixia; after Han Xin was imprisoned and Peng Yue of Liang was executed, he brooded on the peril of a lord who fears his own ministers and on the doom that visits those of one flesh and blood; he devised a scheme to save himself and delay his end, but his army broke in a single battle and he was cut down by Han axes.

manualTranslations.zh: 劉長支庶，奄王大國，承喪亂之餘，禦新化之俗，無德而寵，欲極禍發。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Chang, a collateral branch, suddenly ruled a great state; inheriting the aftermath of disorder and tumult, facing a newly transformed custom—without virtue yet favored, desire reached its limit and disaster erupted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, a cadet of the imperial house, suddenly held a great kingdom; inheriting a realm still raw from chaos and confronting a newly imposed order, he enjoyed favor without virtue until desire ran to excess and ruin broke out.

manualTranslations.zh: 王安內懷先父之憾，外眩奸臣之說，招引賓客，沈溺數術，藉二世之資，恃戈甲之盛，屈強江淮之上，西向而圖宗國，言未絕口，身嗣俱滅。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu An inwardly harbored his late father's grievance, outwardly dazzled by treacherous ministers' persuasions; he drew in guests and retainers, drowned himself in numerology and occult arts, relied on the resources of two generations, trusted in the abundance of weapons and armor, bent force upon the Yangzi and Huai, turned westward and plotted against the imperial house—his words had not ceased when body and heir alike were destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu An nursed his father's old resentment within while beguiled without by crafty advisers; he gathered retainers, immersed himself in numerology and occult arts, drew on the wealth of two reigns, and trusted in vast stores of arms; flexing power along the Yangzi and Huai, he turned west to strike at the imperial domain—and before his design was fully spoken, he and his line were annihilated.

manualTranslations.zh: 李憲因亡新之余，袁術當衰漢之末，負力幸亂，遂生僭逆之計，建號九江，稱制下邑，狼狽奔亡，傾城受戮。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Xian rode the remnant of the fallen Xin; Yuan Shu stood at the end of a declining Han; relying on force and trusting disorder, they then produced plans of usurpation and treason, established a title in Jiujiang, and declared rule over lesser towns; in frantic flight and ruin the whole city suffered execution.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Xian seized on the wreckage of Wang Mang's Xin dynasty; Yuan Shu rose as Han declined; trusting in brute force and welcoming chaos, they hatched treasonous designs, proclaimed a reign in Jiujiang, and asserted rule over subordinate towns—only to flee in disgrace and see their cities leveled and their people slaughtered.

manualTranslations.zh: 及至彥雲、仲恭、公休之徒，或憑宿名，或怙前功，握兵淮楚，力制東夏，屬當多難之世，仍值廢興之會，謀非所議，相系禍敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Down to the likes of Yan Yun, Zhong Gong, and Gong Xiu—some relying on long-standing fame, some presuming on former merit—they grasped armies in Huai and Chu, by force controlled eastern Xia; just when the age was full of hardship, they still met the turning point of ruin and revival; their plots were not what should have been deliberated, and disaster and defeat followed one upon another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then came Wang Ling, Guanqiu Jian, Zhuge Dan, and men of their kind—some trading on old renown, others on past service—who seized armies in the Huai-Chu region and dominated the eastern heartland; in an age already racked by hardship, at the very juncture of dynastic rise and fall, they pursued reckless designs and brought ruin upon one another in succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 祖約助逆，身亡家族。
manualTranslations.literal: Zu Yue aided rebellion; his person perished and his clan was destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zu Yue abetted rebellion and lost both his life and his entire family.

manualTranslations.zh: 彼十亂者，成乎人事者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those ten disorders were accomplished through human affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those ten rebellions were the work of human conduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則侵弱昏迷，以至絕滅，亡楚當之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus then invasion, weakening, and delusion leading to utter extinction—declining Chu bore this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus enfeeblement, confusion, and final extinction fell, as they had upon dying Chu.

manualTranslations.zh: 恃強畏逼，遂謀叛亂，黥布有焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Trusting in strength yet fearing pressure, then plotting rebellion and disorder—Ying Bu was such a case.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Relying on power yet dreading coercion, then turning to rebellion—such was Ying Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 二王遘逆，寵之之過也。
manualTranslations.literal: The two kings encountering treason—this was excess in favor shown them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The two princes who turned traitor did so because favor had been heaped upon them beyond measure.

manualTranslations.zh: 公路僭偽，乘釁之盜也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gonglu's usurpation and false rule was a bandit who seized an opening.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, styled Gonglu, was a usurper who preyed on opportunity.

manualTranslations.zh: 二將以圖功首難，士少以驕矜樂禍。
manualTranslations.literal: Two generals, seeking merit, were first to raise difficulty; lesser officers, through arrogance, delighted in calamity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Two generals courted merit by stirring trouble first; lesser commanders, proud and reckless, welcomed disaster.

manualTranslations.zh: 本其所因，考其成跡，皆寵盛禍淫，福過災生，而制之不漸，積之有由也。
manualTranslations.literal: Tracing what they relied upon and examining the tracks of their accomplishment, all were favor overflowing and disaster following excess, fortune passing its measure and calamity arising—and control was not gradual; accumulation had its causes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tracing their origins and reviewing the record of their deeds, each case shows favor run to excess and disaster bred by overweening fortune; blessings outran their measure and ruin followed, because restraint was never applied gradually and the seeds had long been sown.

manualTranslations.zh: 其下篇曰：昔高祖之誅黥布也，撮三策之要，馳赦過之書，乘人主之威以除逆節之虜，然猶決戰陳都，暴屍橫野，僅乃克之，害亦深矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Its lower chapter says: Formerly, when Gaozu executed Ying Bu, he gathered the essentials of three stratagems, dispatched edicts pardoning past offenses, and rode the sovereign's majesty to remove a rebel of deviant integrity—yet still he fought a decisive battle at the Chen capital, corpses were exposed and strewn across the wilds, and only then was victory achieved; the harm was also deep indeed!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lower essay begins: when Gaozu moved against Ying Bu, he distilled the essentials of three plans, issued amnesties for past crimes, and wielded imperial authority to crush a rebellious foe—yet still he had to fight a decisive battle at the Chen capital, leaving corpses heaped across the plain before victory came; the cost was grievous indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 長安之謀，雖兵未交于山東，禍未遍於天下，而馳說之士與闔境之人幽囚誅放者，亦已眾矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Chang'an conspiracy—though troops had not yet clashed east of the mountains and disaster had not yet spread across the realm, envoys and persuaders together with people throughout the borders who were imprisoned, executed, or exiled were already numerous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Wang Ling's conspiracy, though armies had not yet met east of the mountains and calamity had not engulfed the empire, the persuaders who were sent forth and the people throughout the region who were imprisoned, executed, or banished were already legion.

manualTranslations.zh: 光武連兵于肥舒，魏祖馳馬於蘄苦，而廬九之間流溺兵凶者十而七八焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Guangwu linked armies at Fei and Shu; the Wei founder galloped horses at Qi and Ku; yet between Lu and Jiu those swept away, drowned, or harmed by soldiery were seven or eight in ten.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guangwu campaigned repeatedly in Fei and Shu; Cao Cao drove his armies through Qi and Ku; yet between Lujiang and Jiujiang seven or eight of every ten people were drowned, displaced, or destroyed by war.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫王淩面縛，得之于砎石；
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Ling bound his own face and was obtained at Fancheng;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling came forward with bound face and was taken at Fancheng;

manualTranslations.zh: 仲恭接刃，成之於後覺也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong Gong met the blade, and accomplishment came only through belated awareness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian met the sword, and success came only after rulers awakened too late.

manualTranslations.zh: 而高祖以之宵征，世宗以之發疾，豈不勤哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Gaozu for this made night campaigns; Shizong for this fell ill—were they not diligent!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet Gaozu marched through the night for such ends, and Emperor Wu fell ill from such exertions—were they not tireless!

manualTranslations.zh: 文皇挾萬乘之威，杖伊周之權，內舉京畿之眾，外征四海之銳，雲合雨集，推鋒以臨淮浦，而誕欽晏然，方嬰城自固，憑軾以觀王師。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen wielded the majesty of ten thousand chariots, leaned on the authority of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; inwardly he raised the masses of the capital region, outwardly he summoned the sharp elite of the four seas; clouds gathered and rain converged as he drove his vanguard to the Huai shore—yet Dan and Qin were at ease, just then closing the city to hold firm, leaning on the chariot rail to observe the royal army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen deployed the might of an empire and exercised power like Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou; he mobilized the armies of the capital districts within and the finest troops of the realm without; forces massed like clouds and rain as he pressed the front to the Huai bank—yet Zhuge Dan and Wen Qin remained unruffled, sealing the city and holding fast, leaning on their chariot rails to watch the imperial host.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是築長圍，起棼櫓，高壁連塹，負戈擊柝以守之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon they built a long encirclement, raised tangled siege towers, high walls linked with ditches, and bearing weapons and striking watch-clappers they defended it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the besiegers raised a long encirclement, erected siege towers, linked high walls with trenches, and settled in behind arms and watch-drums to hold the lines.

manualTranslations.zh: 自夏及春，而後始知亡焉。
manualTranslations.literal: From summer until spring, only afterward did they know destruction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From summer through spring the siege dragged on before they at last met their ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則屠城之禍，其可極言乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Thus then the calamity of slaughtering cities—can it be fully told?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for the horror of cities put to the sword, can it even be fully described?

manualTranslations.zh: 約之出奔，淮左為墟，悲夫！
manualTranslations.literal: Yue's flight into exile—the left bank of the Huai became ruins; alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue fled, the country east of the Huai was reduced to wasteland—how lamentable!

manualTranslations.zh: 信哉魯哀之言，夫生乎深宮，長於膏梁，憂懼不切於身，榮辱不交於前，則其仁義之本淺矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Trustworthy indeed are Duke Ai of Lu's words: one born in the deep palace, reared amid fine grain and meat—if worry and fear do not cut close to the person, if honor and disgrace do not meet one face to face, then the root of benevolence and righteousness is shallow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How true were Duke Ai of Lu's words: born deep within the palace and reared on the finest fare, if worry never touches one's person and honor and shame never stand before one's eyes, the roots of benevolence and righteousness must remain shallow.

manualTranslations.zh: 奉以南面之尊，藉以列城之富，宅以制險之居，養以眾強之盛，而無德以臨之，無制以節之，則厭溢樂禍之心生矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Given the honor of facing south, lent the wealth of many cities, dwelling in a residence that commands strategic peril, nourished by the abundance of numerous strength—yet without virtue to oversee it, without regulation to restrain it—then a heart sated to overflow and delighting in calamity is born.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Invested with the throne, endowed with wealthy cities, lodged in a fortress of strategic advantage, and sustained by vast armed strength—yet without virtue to govern and without restraint to curb excess—the mind grows surfeited and begins to relish disaster.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫以昏主禦奸臣，利甲資堅城，偽令行于封內，邪惠結于人心，乘間幸濟之說日交於側，猾詐錮咎之群各馳於前，見利如歸，安在其不為亂乎！
manualTranslations.literal: For a benighted lord to face treacherous ministers, sharp armor supplied by stout walls, false commands running within the fief, wicked favors binding people's hearts—plots that seize openings and hope for success daily meet at one's side; crafty, deceitful bands that lock in blame each race forward; seeing profit they return like homing—how could disorder not arise!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When a dim ruler confronts crafty ministers, when sharp weapons and stout walls become assets, when false decrees rule within the domain and corrupt favors win men's hearts, when daily counsel urges seizing every chance, when deceitful factions press forward, and when men rush toward profit as toward home—how could rebellion not follow!

manualTranslations.zh: 況乘舊寵，挾前功，畏逼懼亡，以謀圖身之舉者，望其俯首就羈，不亦迂哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, for one who rides old favor, clutches former merit, fears pressure and dreads ruin, and undertakes a plot to preserve himself— to expect that he will bow his head and accept bonds, is that not absurd!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: And for men who trade on past favor, brandish old achievements, dread coercion, fear destruction, and scheme for their own survival—to expect them meekly to submit is surely naive.

manualTranslations.zh: 《易》稱「履霜堅冰，馴致之道，」蓋言漸也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Changes says, "Treading frost, solid ice"—the way of gradual arrival—this speaks of gradualness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Frost underfoot means solid ice to come"—the path of gradual development; it is speaking of slow accumulation.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗚呼！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 斯所以亂臣賊子亡國覆家累世而不絕者歟！
manualTranslations.literal: This then is why rebellious ministers and wicked sons destroy states and overturn houses, generation after generation without cease!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is why traitorous ministers and rebellious sons bring down states and ruin families age after age without end!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔先生之宰天下也，選於有德，訪之三吏，正其分位元，明其等級，畫之封疆，宣之政令，上下有序，無僭差之嫌，四人安業，無並兼之國。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly when the sage-kings governed the realm, they selected the virtuous, consulted the three administrators, rectified allotted positions and primary rank, clarified grades and levels, demarcated borders and frontiers, proclaimed policies and commands; high and low had order, without suspicion of overstepping; the four peoples pursued their occupations in peace, and there were no states of annexation and merger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when the sage rulers governed the realm, they chose the virtuous, sought counsel from the chief officers, fixed ranks and stations, defined grades, drew borders, and proclaimed laws; superior and inferior kept their order without trespass; the people in all quarters pursued their callings in peace, and no lord annexed another's domain.

manualTranslations.zh: 三載考陟，功罪不得逃其跡，九伐時修，刑賞無所謬其實。
manualTranslations.literal: Every three years they examined promotion; merit and guilt could not escape their tracks; the nine punitive expeditions were timely maintained; punishments and rewards nowhere missed their true measure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every three years they reviewed appointments, so merit and guilt left a clear record; the nine punitive campaigns were kept in due repair, and rewards and punishments never missed their mark.

manualTranslations.zh: 令之有漸，軌之有度，寵之有節，權不外授，威不下黷，所以杜其萌際，重其名器，深根固本，傳之百世。
manualTranslations.literal: Commands had gradualness, tracks had measure, favor had moderation; authority was not granted outside, majesty was not debased below—thereby to block the first sprouting, to honor titles and regalia, to root deeply and secure the foundation, and to transmit it for a hundred generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Laws advanced step by step, conduct had its proper bounds, and favor knew its limits; power was not delegated rashly, nor was authority cheapened; thus the first signs of disorder were cut off, titles and honors were held in esteem, foundations were sunk deep and made firm, and the state could be handed down for a hundred generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖時有盛衰，弱者無所懼其亡；
manualTranslations.literal: Though times had flourishing and decline, the weak had nothing by which to fear their extinction;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though fortunes rose and fell, the weak need not fear extinction;

manualTranslations.zh: 道有興廢，強者不得資其弊。
manualTranslations.literal: the Way had rise and abandonment, and the strong could not rely on such weakness for advantage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and though the Way itself might wax or wane, the strong could not exploit disorder for private gain.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫如是，將使天下從風，穆然軌道，慶自一人，惠流萬國，安有向時之患哉！
manualTranslations.literal: If it were thus, it would make the realm follow like the wind, solemnly keep to the proper track, felicity arise from one man, grace flow to ten thousand states—how could there be the troubles of former times!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Were it so, the empire would follow as if on the wind, move solemnly along the right path, draw its blessings from a single ruler, and spread his grace to every state—what room would remain for the calamities of ages past!

sourceRange.text: 後為《三國名臣頌》曰：夫百姓不能自牧，故立君以治之；明君不能獨治，則為臣以佐之。然則三五迭隆，歷代承基，揖讓之與干戈，文德之與武功，莫不宗匠陶鈞而群才緝熙，元首經略而股肱肆力。雖遭罹不同，跡有優劣，至於體分冥固，道契不墜，風美所扇，訓革千載，其揆一也。故二八升而唐朝盛，伊呂用而湯武寧，三賢進而小白興，五臣顯而重耳霸。中古陵遲，斯道替矣。居上者不以至公理物，為下者必以私路期榮，禦員者不以信誠率眾，執方者必以權謀自顯。於是君臣離而名教薄，世多亂而時不治，故蘧寧以之卷舒，柳下以之三黜，接輿以之行歌，魯連以之赴海。衰世之中，保持名節，君臣相體，若合符契，則燕昭、樂毅古之流矣。夫未遇伯樂，則千載無一驥；時值龍顏，則當年控三傑，漢之得賢，於斯為貴。高祖雖不以道勝禦物，群下得盡其忠；蕭曹雖不以三代事主，百姓不失其業。靜亂庇人，抑亦其次。夫時方顛沛，則顯不如隱；萬物思治，則默不如語。是以古之君子不患弘道難，患遭時難；遭時匪難，遇君難。故有道無時，孟子所以咨嗟；有時無君，賈生所以垂泣。夫萬歲一期，有生之通塗；千載一遇，賢智之嘉會。遇之不能無欣，喪之何能無慨。古人之言，信有情哉！余以暇日常覽《國志》，考其君臣，比其行事，雖道謝先代，亦異世一時也。文若懷獨見之照，而有救世之心，論時則人方塗炭，計能則莫出魏武，故委圖霸朝，豫謀世事。舉才不以標鑒，故人亡而後顯；籌畫不以要功，故事至而後定。雖亡身明順，識亦高矣。董卓之亂，神器遷逼，公達慨然，志在致命。由斯而譚，故以大存名節。至如身為漢隸而跡入魏幕，源流趣舍，抑亦文若之謂。所以存亡殊致，始終不同，將以文若既明且哲，名教有寄乎！夫仁義不可不明，時宗舉其致；生理不可不全，故達識攝其契。相與弘道，豈不遠哉！崔生高朗，折而不撓，所以策名魏武、執笏霸朝者，蓋以漢主當陽，魏後北面者哉！若乃一旦進璽，君臣易位，則崔生所以不與，魏氏所以不容。夫江湖所以濟舟，亦所以覆舟；仁義所以全身，亦所以亡身。然而先賢玉摧于前，來哲攘袂於後，豈天懷發中，而名教束物者乎！孔明盤桓，俟時而動，遐想管樂，遠明風流，治國以禮，人無怨聲，刑罰不濫，沒有餘泣，雖古之遺愛，何以加茲！及其臨終顧托，受遺作相，劉後授之無疑心，武侯受之無懼色，繼體納之無貳情，百姓信之無異辭，君臣之際，良可詠矣！公瑾卓爾，逸志不群，總角料主，則素契于伯符；晚節曜奇，則三分於赤壁。惜其齡促，志未可量。子布佐策，致延譽之美，輟哭止哀，有翼戴之功，神情所涉，豈徒謇諤而已哉！然杜門不用，登壇受譏。夫一人之身所照未異，而用舍之間俄有不同，況沈跡溝壑，遇與不遇者乎！夫詩頌之作，有自來矣。或以吟詠情性，或以紀德顯功，雖大指同歸，所托或乖。若夫出處有道，名體不滯，風軌德音，為世作範，不可廢也。復綴序所懷，以為之贊曰：火德既微，運纏大過。洪飆扇海，二溟揚波。虯獸雖驚，風雲未和。潛魚擇川，高鳥候柯。赫赫三雄，並回乾軸。競收杞梓，爭采松竹。鳳不及棲，龍不暇伏。谷無幽蘭，嶺無停菊。英英文若，靈鑒洞照。應變知微，頤奇賞要。日月在躬，隱之彌曜。文明暎心，贊之愈妙。滄海橫流，玉石俱碎。達人兼善，廢己存愛。謀解時紛，功濟宇內。始救生靈，終明風概。公達潛朗，思同蓍蔡。運用無方，動攝群會。爰初發跡，遘此顛沛。神情玄定，處之彌泰。愔愔幕裹，算無不經亹癖通韻，跡不暫停。雖懷尺璧，顧哂連城。智能極物，愚足全生。郎中溫雅，器識純素。貞而不諒，通而能固。恂恂德心，汪汪軌度。仁者必勇，德亦有言。雖遇履尾，神氣恬然。行不修飾，名節無愆。操不激切，素風愈鮮。邈哉崔生，體正心直。天骨疏朗，牆岸高嶷。忠存軌跡，義形風色。思樹芳蘭，翦除荊棘。人惡其上，世不容哲。琅琅先生，雅杖名節。雖遇塵務，猶震霜雪。運極道消，碎此明月。景山恢誕，韻與道合。形器不存，方寸海納。和而不同，通而不雜。遇醉忘辭，在醒貽答。長文通雅，義格終始。思戴元首，擬伊同恥。人未知德，懼若在己。嘉謀肆庭，讜言盈耳。玉生雖麗，光不逾把。德積雖微，道暎天下。邈哉太初，宇量高雅。器范自然。標準無假。全身由直，跡洿必偽。處死匪難，理存則易。萬物波蕩，孰任其累！六合徒廣，容身靡寄。君親自然，匪由名教。愛敬既同，情禮兼到。烈烈王生，知死不撓。求仁不遠，期在忠存。玄伯剛簡，大存名體。端委獸門，正言彌啟。臨危致命，盡其心禮。堂堂孔明，基宇宏邈。器同生靈，獨稟先覺。標榜風流，遠明管樂。初九龍盤，雅志彌確。百六道喪，干戈迭用。苟非命世，孰掃雰雺！宗子思甯，薄言解控。釋褐中林，郁為時棟。士元弘長，雅性內融。崇善愛物，觀始知終。喪亂備矣。勝塗未隆。先生標之，振起清風。綢繆哲後，無妄惟時。夙夜匪懈，義在緝熙。三略既陳，霸業已基。公琰殖根，不忘中正。豈曰模擬，實在雅性。亦既羈勒，負荷時命。推賢恭己，久而可敬。公衡沖達，秉志淵塞。媚茲一人，臨難不惑。疇昔不造，假翮鄰國。進能徽音，退不失德。六合紛紜，人心將變。鳥擇高梧，臣須顧眄。公瑾英達，朗心獨見。披草求君，定交一面。桓桓魏武，外托霸跡。卓卓若人，曜奇赤壁。三光參分，宇宙暫隔。子布擅名，遭世方擾。撫翼桑梓，息肩江表。王略威夷，吳魏同寶。遂贊宏謨，匡此霸道。桓王之薨，大業未純。把臂托孤，惟賢與親。轟哭止哀，臨難忘身。成此南面，實由老臣。才為世生，世亦須才。得而能任，貴在無猜。昂昂子敬，拔跡草萊。荷簷吐奇，乃構雲臺。子瑜都長，體性純懿。諫而不犯，正而不毅。將命公庭，退忘私位。豈無鶺鴒，固慎名器。伯言謇謇，以道佐世。出能勤功，入亦獻替。謀寧社稷，妥紛挫銳。正以招疑，忠而獲戾。元歎邈遠，神和形檢。如彼白珪，質無塵點。立行以恆，匡主以漸。清不增潔，濁不加染。仲翔高亮，性不和物。好是不群，折而不屈。屢摧逆鱗，直道受黜。歎過孫陽，放同賈屈。莘莘眾賢，千載一遇。整轡高衢，驤首天路。仰揖玄流，俯弘時務。名節殊塗，雅致同趣。日月麗天，瞻之不墜。仁義在躬，用之不匱。尚想遐風，載揖載味。後生擊節，懦夫增氣。

manualTranslations.zh: 後為《三國名臣頌》曰：夫百姓不能自牧，故立君以治之；
manualTranslations.literal: Later he composed the 'Panegyric on Eminent Ministers of the Three Kingdoms,' saying: The common people cannot govern themselves, so a ruler is established to govern them;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later wrote the Panegyric on Eminent Ministers of the Three Kingdoms, which begins: The people cannot govern themselves, and so a ruler is set up to rule them;

manualTranslations.zh: 明君不能獨治，則為臣以佐之。
manualTranslations.literal: a bright ruler cannot govern alone, so ministers are appointed to assist him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: a wise ruler cannot rule alone, and ministers are appointed to aid him.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則三五迭隆，歷代承基，揖讓之與干戈，文德之與武功，莫不宗匠陶鈞而群才緝熙，元首經略而股肱肆力。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors rose in turn, each age inheriting the foundation; whether by abdication or by arms, by civil virtue or martial achievement, none failed to have a master craftsman shape and mold while many talents gathered in splendor, the head planning strategy while arms and legs exerted their strength.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus through the ages of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, each dynasty inherited the throne; whether by peaceful succession or by war, by civil culture or martial prowess, a master craftsman always shaped the age while many talents flourished together, the sovereign laying plans and his ministers giving their full strength.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖遭罹不同，跡有優劣，至於體分冥固，道契不墜，風美所扇，訓革千載，其揆一也。
manualTranslations.literal: Though their sufferings differed and their tracks had better and worse, as to the substance of their roles being obscurely firm, their accord with the Way not falling, the beauty they fanned abroad, and their teaching reforming a thousand years—their measure was one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though their fortunes differed and their records were unequal, in the firmness of their roles, the steadfastness of their bond with the Way, the moral beauty they spread, and the lessons that reformed the ages, their standard was the same.

manualTranslations.zh: 故二八升而唐朝盛，伊呂用而湯武寧，三賢進而小白興，五臣顯而重耳霸。
manualTranslations.literal: Hence when the Eight and the Twenty rose, the Tang dynasty flourished; when Yi and Lü were employed, Tang and Wu were pacified; when three worthies advanced, Duke Huan of Qi rose; when five ministers appeared, Duke Wen of Jin became hegemon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus when the Eight and the Twenty took office, the house of Tang prospered; when Yi Yin and Lü Shang were used, Tang and Wu knew peace; when three worthies advanced, Duke Huan rose; when five ministers stood forth, Duke Wen of Jin achieved hegemony.

manualTranslations.zh: 中古陵遲，斯道替矣。
manualTranslations.literal: In middle antiquity decline set in, and this Way fell away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the middle ages the age declined, and this principle was lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 居上者不以至公理物，為下者必以私路期榮，禦員者不以信誠率眾，執方者必以權謀自顯。
manualTranslations.literal: Those above did not use utmost fairness to order things; those below were sure to seek glory by private paths; those steering the course did not lead the masses with trust and sincerity; those holding the compass were sure to display themselves through schemes for power.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those in high place no longer governed all things with perfect fairness; those below sought advancement by private means; those at the helm did not lead the people with sincerity; those who held authority displayed themselves through intrigue.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是君臣離而名教薄，世多亂而時不治，故蘧寧以之卷舒，柳下以之三黜，接輿以之行歌，魯連以之赴海。
manualTranslations.literal: Then ruler and minister parted and name-and-teaching grew thin; the age had much disorder and the times were not governed; hence Qu Ning by it drew in and spread out, Liu Xia Hui by it suffered three dismissals, Jie Yu by it went singing, and Lu Zhonglian by it went to the sea.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then lord and minister were estranged and moral teaching grew thin; the age was chaotic and order failed; and so Qu Ning withdrew and returned, Liu Xia Hui was thrice dismissed, Jie Yu went about singing, and Lu Zhonglian threw himself into the sea.

manualTranslations.zh: 衰世之中，保持名節，君臣相體，若合符契，則燕昭、樂毅古之流矣。
manualTranslations.literal: In a declining age, to preserve name and integrity, ruler and minister mutually embodying each other as if matching tallies—such were the ancient stream of King Zhao of Yan and Yue Yi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In a decadent age, to preserve integrity and have ruler and minister embody one another as though joined by a tally—that was the ancient pattern of King Zhao of Yan and Yue Yi.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫未遇伯樂，則千載無一驥；
manualTranslations.literal: If one has not met a Bo Le, then in a thousand years there is not one swift steed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without meeting a Bo Le, a thousand years may pass without a single swift steed;

manualTranslations.zh: 時值龍顏，則當年控三傑，漢之得賢，於斯為貴。
manualTranslations.literal: when the time met a dragon countenance, then in that very year three heroes were reined in—the Han's gaining worthies was precious in this respect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: but when the age met a dragon countenance, three heroes were harnessed in a single generation; in this lay the Han's true treasure of worthy men.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖雖不以道勝禦物，群下得盡其忠；
manualTranslations.literal: Though Emperor Gaozu did not overcome things by the Way in ruling, the host below could exhaust their loyalty;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Gaozu did not rule by triumph of the Way over things, his followers could give their full loyalty;

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭曹雖不以三代事主，百姓不失其業。
manualTranslations.literal: though Xiao and Cao did not serve lords of the Three Dynasties, the common people did not lose their occupations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and though Xiao He and Cao Shen did not serve lords of the Three Dynasties, the people did not lose their livelihoods.

manualTranslations.zh: 靜亂庇人，抑亦其次。
manualTranslations.literal: Pacifying disorder and sheltering the people—this too was secondary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To still chaos and shelter the people was, after all, a lesser matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫時方顛沛，則顯不如隱；
manualTranslations.literal: When the time was in turmoil, then showing oneself was not as good as hiding;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the age was in turmoil, to stand forth was inferior to withdrawal;

manualTranslations.zh: 萬物思治，則默不如語。
manualTranslations.literal: when all things longed for order, then silence was not as good as speech.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when all things yearned for order, silence was inferior to speaking out.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以古之君子不患弘道難，患遭時難；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the gentlemen of old did not worry that spreading the Way was hard; they worried that meeting the time was hard;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the gentlemen of old did not fear that spreading the Way was difficult; they feared that the times were difficult;

manualTranslations.zh: 遭時匪難，遇君難。
manualTranslations.literal: if meeting the time was not hard, meeting the ruler was hard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and if the times were not hard, meeting the right ruler was hard.

manualTranslations.zh: 故有道無時，孟子所以咨嗟；
manualTranslations.literal: Hence having the Way but not the time is why Mencius sighed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence Mencius sighed because he had the Way but not the time;

manualTranslations.zh: 有時無君，賈生所以垂泣。
manualTranslations.literal: having the time but not the ruler is why Master Jia shed tears.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and Jia Yi wept because he had the time but not the ruler.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫萬歲一期，有生之通塗；
manualTranslations.literal: Ten thousand years make one term—the common path of life;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ten thousand years form one span—the common road of life;

manualTranslations.zh: 千載一遇，賢智之嘉會。
manualTranslations.literal: a thousand years bring one meeting—the fine assembly of the worthy and wise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: a meeting once in a thousand years—the splendid occasion of the worthy and wise.

manualTranslations.zh: 遇之不能無欣，喪之何能無慨。
manualTranslations.literal: To meet it one cannot be without joy; to lose it how can one be without sighing?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To meet such a moment brings joy; to lose it brings sighs—how could it be otherwise?

manualTranslations.zh: 古人之言，信有情哉！
manualTranslations.literal: The words of the ancients—truly full of feeling!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The words of the ancients are truly charged with feeling!

manualTranslations.zh: 余以暇日常覽《國志》，考其君臣，比其行事，雖道謝先代，亦異世一時也。
manualTranslations.literal: I in my leisure days often perused the Records of the Three Kingdoms, examined its rulers and ministers, and compared their conduct; though the Way fell short of earlier ages, it was still one moment in another age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In my leisure I often read the Records of the Three Kingdoms, studying its rulers and ministers and comparing their deeds; though their Way fell short of earlier ages, they were nonetheless a moment unto themselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 文若懷獨見之照，而有救世之心，論時則人方塗炭，計能則莫出魏武，故委圖霸朝，豫謀世事。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenruo bore the illumination of unique insight and had a heart to save the age; considering the time, men were just in charcoal and paste; reckoning ability, none surpassed Wei Wu—hence he entrusted his plans to the hegemonic court and foresaw affairs of the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yu possessed the light of singular insight and a heart set on saving the age; the people were in misery, and in ability none surpassed Cao Cao; so he entrusted his designs to the hegemonic court and planned ahead for the affairs of the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 舉才不以標鑒，故人亡而後顯；
manualTranslations.literal: In raising talent he did not use labels and mirrors, so men became illustrious only after death;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He recommended talent without keeping score, so men became famous only after they died;

manualTranslations.zh: 籌畫不以要功，故事至而後定。
manualTranslations.literal: in planning he did not demand merit, so affairs were settled only when they arrived.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he planned without demanding credit, so affairs were settled only when they came to fruition.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖亡身明順，識亦高矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Though he lost his life in clarifying submission, his discernment was also lofty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though he lost his life in making clear his submission, his insight was lofty indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 董卓之亂，神器遷逼，公達慨然，志在致命。
manualTranslations.literal: In Dong Zhuo's rebellion, the sacred vessel was forced to move; Gongda sighed deeply, his aim set on giving his life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Dong Zhuo's rebellion, when the imperial regalia was seized, Sima Yi was stirred with resolve to give his life.

manualTranslations.zh: 由斯而譚，故以大存名節。
manualTranslations.literal: From this to speak of it, he thereby preserved name and integrity on a great scale.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, he preserved his integrity on the grandest scale.

manualTranslations.zh: 至如身為漢隸而跡入魏幕，源流趣舍，抑亦文若之謂。
manualTranslations.literal: As for being in body a subject of Han while one's tracks entered Wei's tent—the source and flow, inclination and choice—this too may be said of Wenruo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for serving in body as a subject of Han while one's path entered Wei's camp—in source, course, and choice, this may also be said of Xun Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 所以存亡殊致，始終不同，將以文若既明且哲，名教有寄乎！
manualTranslations.literal: The reason survival and destruction had different ends and beginning and end were not the same must be that Wenruo was both bright and wise, and that name-and-teaching had a lodging in him!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That survival and destruction took different courses and beginnings and ends diverged must be because Xun Yu was bright and wise, and moral teaching found its lodging in him!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫仁義不可不明，時宗舉其致；
manualTranslations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness cannot go unclarified; the age's exemplars raised up their attainment;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness must be made clear; the age's exemplars displayed their fulfillment;

manualTranslations.zh: 生理不可不全，故達識攝其契。
manualTranslations.literal: the principle of life cannot go unfulfilled; hence the far-seeing took up its bond.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the principle of preserving life must be kept whole; hence the far-seeing grasped its inner bond.

manualTranslations.zh: 相與弘道，豈不遠哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Together to spread the Way—is it not far-reaching!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Together to spread the Way—was that not a far-reaching aim!

manualTranslations.zh: 崔生高朗，折而不撓，所以策名魏武、執笏霸朝者，蓋以漢主當陽，魏後北面者哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Master Cui was lofty and bright, broken yet unbending; the reason he inscribed his name with Wei Wu and held the tablet in the hegemonic court was surely that the Han lord faced the sun and the Wei ruler stood to the north!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cui Yan was lofty and bright, broken yet unbending; the reason he took office under Cao Cao and held court at the hegemon's side was surely that the Han sovereign still faced the south while the Wei ruler stood to the north!

manualTranslations.zh: 若乃一旦進璽，君臣易位，則崔生所以不與，魏氏所以不容。
manualTranslations.literal: If in a single day the seal were advanced and ruler and minister exchanged places, then that is why Master Cui would not join in and why the house of Wei could not tolerate him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But had the imperial seal been offered in a day and ruler and minister changed places, that is why Cui Yan would not have joined in, and why Wei could not tolerate him.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫江湖所以濟舟，亦所以覆舟；
manualTranslations.literal: Rivers and lakes can ferry a boat, and can also overturn a boat;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rivers and lakes can carry a boat, and they can also overturn one;

manualTranslations.zh: 仁義所以全身，亦所以亡身。
manualTranslations.literal: benevolence and righteousness can preserve the body, and can also destroy the body.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: benevolence and righteousness can preserve the body, and they can also destroy it.

manualTranslations.zh: 然而先賢玉摧于前，來哲攘袂於後，豈天懷發中，而名教束物者乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet former worthies were jade-shattered before, and later sages rolled up their sleeves after—was it not Heaven's intent issuing from within, and name-and-teaching binding things!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet former worthies were shattered like jade before, and later sages rolled up their sleeves after—was this not Heaven's intent welling from within, and moral teaching binding men to their duty!

manualTranslations.zh: 孔明盤桓，俟時而動，遐想管樂，遠明風流，治國以禮，人無怨聲，刑罰不濫，沒有餘泣，雖古之遺愛，何以加茲！
manualTranslations.literal: Kongming lingered and turned, waiting for the time to act; he looked far to Guan and Yue and illumined elegance from afar; he governed the state by ritual, men had no sounds of complaint, punishments were not excessive, and at death there were no leftover tears—though the cherished love of antiquity, how could one add to this!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang lingered in seclusion, waiting for the right moment; he looked back to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi and carried their elegance far forward; he governed by ritual, the people murmured no complaint, punishments were not abused, and at death none wept in vain—what ancient beloved minister could surpass this!

manualTranslations.zh: 及其臨終顧托，受遺作相，劉後授之無疑心，武侯受之無懼色，繼體納之無貳情，百姓信之無異辭，君臣之際，良可詠矣！
manualTranslations.literal: When at his end he looked back in entrustment, received the testament and became chief minister—the Later Lord entrusted him without doubting heart, the Martial Lord received it without fearful countenance, the heir accepted it without divided feeling, the common people trusted it without differing words; the juncture of ruler and minister—truly fit for song!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At his deathbed he entrusted the realm and became chief minister; Empress Liu entrusted him without doubt, Zhuge Liang received the charge without fear, the heir accepted it without disloyalty, and the people believed without dissent—the bond between ruler and minister is truly worth celebrating in song!

manualTranslations.zh: 公瑾卓爾，逸志不群，總角料主，則素契于伯符；
manualTranslations.literal: Gongjin stood out alone, his free ambition unmatched; from boyhood he gauged his lord, and was long in accord with Bofu;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu stood apart in excellence, his free spirit unmatched; from youth he judged his lord and was long bound to Sun Ce;

manualTranslations.zh: 晚節曜奇，則三分於赤壁。
manualTranslations.literal: in his later years his brilliance was wondrous, and the realm was divided threefold at Red Cliffs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: in his later years his brilliance flared, and at Red Cliffs the realm was divided threefold.

manualTranslations.zh: 惜其齡促，志未可量。
manualTranslations.literal: Pity that his years were short; his ambition could not be measured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas that his years were brief; his ambition cannot be measured.

manualTranslations.zh: 子布佐策，致延譽之美，輟哭止哀，有翼戴之功，神情所涉，豈徒謇諤而已哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Zibu assisted in planning, achieving the beauty of prolonged praise; he ceased weeping and stopped mourning, and had the merit of winging and upholding; what his spirit and bearing touched—was it only blunt remonstrance!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Su aided in planning and won lasting renown; he stopped the mourning and had the merit of supporting the throne; what his spirit and bearing touched went far beyond mere blunt remonstrance!

manualTranslations.zh: 然杜門不用，登壇受譏。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet he shut his gates and was not employed, and mounting the altar he received ridicule.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet he was shut behind closed doors and unused, and when he mounted the altar he met with ridicule.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫一人之身所照未異，而用舍之間俄有不同，況沈跡溝壑，遇與不遇者乎！
manualTranslations.literal: One man's body—the light it casts is not different, yet between use and rejection there suddenly are differences; how much more for those sunk in ditches and gullies, the met and the unmet!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The same man's light does not change, yet between employment and rejection there may suddenly be a difference—how much more for those sunk in obscurity, the favored and the overlooked!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫詩頌之作，有自來矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The making of odes and panegyrics has had its origin from of old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The writing of odes and panegyrics is an ancient practice.

manualTranslations.zh: 或以吟詠情性，或以紀德顯功，雖大指同歸，所托或乖。
manualTranslations.literal: Some use them to chant and sing one's nature and feelings, some to record virtue and display merit; though the great aim returns to one, what they rest upon may differ.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some sing to give voice to feeling, others record virtue and display merit; though the broad aim is one, what they rest upon may differ.

manualTranslations.zh: 若夫出處有道，名體不滯，風軌德音，為世作範，不可廢也。
manualTranslations.literal: As for advancing and withdrawing having a Way, name and substance not stagnating, model conduct and virtuous repute making a pattern for the age—these cannot be abandoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When advancement and withdrawal follow the Way, when name and substance are not fixed in place, when conduct and reputation serve as models for the age—these cannot be abandoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 復綴序所懷，以為之贊曰：火德既微，運纏大過。
manualTranslations.literal: Again I string together what I harbor in the preface and make for it a praise, saying: The fire virtue was already faint; fortune was entangled in Great Excess.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I now gather what I expressed in the preface and offer this praise: The fire virtue had waned; fate was wound in Great Excess.

manualTranslations.zh: 洪飆扇海，二溟揚波。
manualTranslations.literal: Great gales fanned the sea; the two oceans raised their waves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mighty winds lashed the sea; both oceans heaved their waves.

manualTranslations.zh: 虯獸雖驚，風雲未和。
manualTranslations.literal: Horned beasts were startled, yet wind and cloud were not yet in harmony.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Horned beasts were alarmed, yet wind and cloud had not yet joined in harmony.

manualTranslations.zh: 潛魚擇川，高鳥候柯。
manualTranslations.literal: Hidden fish chose their streams; high birds awaited their branches.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fish in the depths chose their streams; birds on high awaited their branches.

manualTranslations.zh: 赫赫三雄，並回乾軸。
manualTranslations.literal: Brilliant, brilliant—the three heroes together turned the axis of heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Resplendent, the three heroes together turned the axis of heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 競收杞梓，爭采松竹。
manualTranslations.literal: They vied to gather catalpa and cedar; they strove to pluck pine and bamboo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They raced to gather fine timber; they strove to harvest pine and bamboo.

manualTranslations.zh: 鳳不及棲，龍不暇伏。
manualTranslations.literal: The phoenix had no time to perch; the dragon no leisure to crouch.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The phoenix had no branch left to perch on; the dragon no moment to lie low.

manualTranslations.zh: 谷無幽蘭，嶺無停菊。
manualTranslations.literal: In valleys there was no hidden orchid; on ridges no resting chrysanthemum.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No hidden orchids remained in the valleys; no chrysanthemums lingered on the ridges.

manualTranslations.zh: 英英文若，靈鑒洞照。
manualTranslations.literal: Illustrious, illustrious Wenruo—spiritual mirror penetrating in illumination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Illustrious Xun Yu—his discerning mirror pierced all things.

manualTranslations.zh: 應變知微，頤奇賞要。
manualTranslations.literal: Responding to change he knew the subtle; he nourished the wondrous and prized the essential.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He met change and knew the subtle; he cherished the rare and valued the essential.

manualTranslations.zh: 日月在躬，隱之彌曜。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun and moon were in his person; the more he hid, the brighter he shone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun and moon seemed embodied in him; the more he withdrew, the brighter he shone.

manualTranslations.zh: 文明暎心，贊之愈妙。
manualTranslations.literal: Civil brilliance mirrored his heart; the more one praised, the finer it grew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Civil brilliance lit his heart; the more one praised him, the finer he seemed.

manualTranslations.zh: 滄海橫流，玉石俱碎。
manualTranslations.literal: The blue sea flowed crosswise; jade and stone were shattered together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the dark sea flowed awry, jade and common stone were shattered alike.

manualTranslations.zh: 達人兼善，廢己存愛。
manualTranslations.literal: The accomplished man was doubly good; he set himself aside and preserved love.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The far-seeing man embraced all in goodness; he set himself aside and kept love alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 謀解時紛，功濟宇內。
manualTranslations.literal: His plans untied the age's tangles; his merit aided all within the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His counsel unraveled the age's turmoil; his merit aided all within the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 始救生靈，終明風概。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he saved the living masses; at the end he clarified wind and bearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first he saved the people; at the end he made his moral bearing clear.

manualTranslations.zh: 公達潛朗，思同蓍蔡。
manualTranslations.literal: Gongda was hidden yet bright; his thought matched tortoise and milfoil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi was reserved yet luminous; his thought matched the oracle tortoise and milfoil.

manualTranslations.zh: 運用無方，動攝群會。
manualTranslations.literal: In deployment he had no fixed method; in movement he gathered all assemblies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He deployed without fixed method; in action he commanded every assembly.

manualTranslations.zh: 爰初發跡，遘此顛沛。
manualTranslations.literal: When first he set out on his path, he met this turmoil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When first he rose to prominence, he met this age of turmoil.

manualTranslations.zh: 神情玄定，處之彌泰。
manualTranslations.literal: His spirit and bearing were darkly settled; the more he dwelt in it, the more at peace he was.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His spirit was serenely fixed; the more he faced turmoil, the more at ease he grew.

manualTranslations.zh: 愔愔幕裹，算無不經亹癖通韻，跡不暫停。
manualTranslations.literal: Quiet, quiet within the tent-wrap; in calculation nothing went unthreaded, diligently penetrating in resonance, his tracks never briefly halted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Quiet within the tent, in counsel nothing went unconsidered; diligent and penetrating in design, his course never briefly paused.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖懷尺璧，顧哂連城。
manualTranslations.literal: Though he held a foot-long jade disk, he looked back with a smile at cities linked in worth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though he held a foot of jade, he smiled at cities worth a thousand.

manualTranslations.zh: 智能極物，愚足全生。
manualTranslations.literal: Wisdom can exhaust things; folly is enough to preserve life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wisdom may master all things; folly is enough to preserve one's life.

manualTranslations.zh: 郎中溫雅，器識純素。
manualTranslations.literal: The Palace Attendant was mild and elegant; vessel and insight pure and plain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao was mild and refined; his character and insight were pure and plain.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞而不諒，通而能固。
manualTranslations.literal: Upright yet not narrow; penetrating yet able to be firm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Upright yet not rigid; penetrating yet steadfast.

manualTranslations.zh: 恂恂德心，汪汪軌度。
manualTranslations.literal: Deferential, deferential in moral heart; vast, vast in model measure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deferential in moral heart; vast in standard and measure.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁者必勇，德亦有言。
manualTranslations.literal: The benevolent man is sure to be brave; virtue also has its saying.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The benevolent are surely brave; virtue too has its word.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖遇履尾，神氣恬然。
manualTranslations.literal: Though he met treading the tail, his spirit and bearing were tranquil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though he trod the tiger's tail, his spirit remained serene.

manualTranslations.zh: 行不修飾，名節無愆。
manualTranslations.literal: In conduct he did not adorn himself; in name and integrity there was no fault.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He did not adorn his conduct; his integrity knew no fault.

manualTranslations.zh: 操不激切，素風愈鮮。
manualTranslations.literal: His bearing was not sharp and urgent; his plain wind grew fresher.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His manner was not harsh; his plain integrity grew ever fresher.

manualTranslations.zh: 邈哉崔生，體正心直。
manualTranslations.literal: Remote, Master Cui—substance upright, heart straight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Far-seeing Cui Yan—upright in body, straight in heart.

manualTranslations.zh: 天骨疏朗，牆岸高嶷。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's bones were open and bright; his wall-bank was high and steep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven's bone-structure was open and bright; his bearing stood high and steep as a wall.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠存軌跡，義形風色。
manualTranslations.literal: Loyalty lodged in his tracks; righteousness took form in his wind and countenance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Loyalty lived in his every step; righteousness showed in his bearing and face.

manualTranslations.zh: 思樹芳蘭，翦除荊棘。
manualTranslations.literal: He thought to plant fragrant orchids and cut away brambles and thorns.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sought to plant fragrant orchids and cut away thorns.

manualTranslations.zh: 人惡其上，世不容哲。
manualTranslations.literal: Men hated one above them; the age could not tolerate the wise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men resented his uprightness; the age could not tolerate the wise.

manualTranslations.zh: 琅琅先生，雅杖名節。
manualTranslations.literal: Clear-ringing, the Master—elegantly he leaned on name and integrity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Clear-voiced Master Chen—he nobly upheld integrity.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖遇塵務，猶震霜雪。
manualTranslations.literal: Though he met dusty affairs, he still quaked like frost and snow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though he met the dust of office, he still stood firm as frost and snow.

manualTranslations.zh: 運極道消，碎此明月。
manualTranslations.literal: Fortune reached its limit and the Way faded; this bright moon was shattered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When fortune peaked the Way waned; this bright moon was shattered.

manualTranslations.zh: 景山恢誕，韻與道合。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingshan was broad and far-reaching; his resonance joined with the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Kui was broad and far-reaching; his tone harmonized with the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 形器不存，方寸海納。
manualTranslations.literal: Form and vessel did not remain; within a square inch the sea was received.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Form and vessel did not confine him; within a square inch he held the sea.

manualTranslations.zh: 和而不同，通而不雜。
manualTranslations.literal: Harmonious yet not the same; penetrating yet not mixed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Harmonious yet not uniform; penetrating yet not confused.

manualTranslations.zh: 遇醉忘辭，在醒貽答。
manualTranslations.literal: Meeting drunkenness he forgot words; when sober he left answers behind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In drink he forgot fine speech; sober, he left counsel behind.

manualTranslations.zh: 長文通雅，義格終始。
manualTranslations.literal: Changwen was penetrating and refined; righteousness framed beginning and end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Qun was penetrating and refined; righteousness shaped his whole course.

manualTranslations.zh: 思戴元首，擬伊同恥。
manualTranslations.literal: He thought to uphold the chief; he matched Yi in shared shame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sought to uphold the sovereign; he shared Yi Yin's sense of shame.

manualTranslations.zh: 人未知德，懼若在己。
manualTranslations.literal: When men did not yet know virtue, his fear was as if in himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When others failed to know virtue, he feared as though the fault were his own.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉謀肆庭，讜言盈耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Fine plans filled the court; forthright words filled the ears.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fine counsel filled the court; forthright words filled the ears.

manualTranslations.zh: 玉生雖麗，光不逾把。
manualTranslations.literal: Though jade born is beautiful, its light does not exceed a handful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though jade newly born is fair, its light does not pass a hand's breadth.

manualTranslations.zh: 德積雖微，道暎天下。
manualTranslations.literal: Though virtue accumulated is slight, the Way illumines all under heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though virtue gathered may be slight, the Way illumines all under heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 邈哉太初，宇量高雅。
manualTranslations.literal: Remote, Tai Chu—his universe-measure was lofty and elegant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Far-seeing Xi Zheng—his breadth of mind was lofty and refined.

manualTranslations.zh: 器范自然。
manualTranslations.literal: Vessel and model were natural.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His character and model were wholly natural.

manualTranslations.zh: 標準無假。
manualTranslations.literal: Standard and rule had no falsehood.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His standard was without pretense.

manualTranslations.zh: 全身由直，跡洿必偽。
manualTranslations.literal: Preserving the body comes through uprightness; tracks stained must be false.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Preserving the body comes through uprightness; a stained path must be false.

manualTranslations.zh: 處死匪難，理存則易。
manualTranslations.literal: Facing death is not hard; where principle exists it is easy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Facing death is not hard; where principle stands, it is easy.

manualTranslations.zh: 萬物波蕩，孰任其累！
manualTranslations.literal: All things billow and surge—who can bear their burden!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All things surge and toss—who can bear their burden!

manualTranslations.zh: 六合徒廣，容身靡寄。
manualTranslations.literal: The six directions are only vast; a place for the body has nowhere to lodge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The six directions are vast indeed, yet nowhere could his body find rest.

manualTranslations.zh: 君親自然，匪由名教。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord and parent are natural; they are not from name-and-teaching.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sovereign and parent are natural bonds, not mere products of moral teaching.

manualTranslations.zh: 愛敬既同，情禮兼到。
manualTranslations.literal: Love and reverence being alike, feeling and ritual both arrived.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Love and reverence were one; feeling and ritual both were fulfilled.

manualTranslations.zh: 烈烈王生，知死不撓。
manualTranslations.literal: Fierce, fierce Master Wang—knowing death, he did not bend.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fierce Wang Xiang—knowing death, he did not bend.

manualTranslations.zh: 求仁不遠，期在忠存。
manualTranslations.literal: To seek benevolence is not far; the expectation lies in loyalty preserved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To seek benevolence is not far; it rests in keeping loyalty alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄伯剛簡，大存名體。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuanbo was firm and plain; on a great scale he preserved name and substance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Jiao was firm and plain; on the grand scale he preserved name and substance.

manualTranslations.zh: 端委獸門，正言彌啟。
manualTranslations.literal: With correct robe at the beast gate, upright words ever more opened forth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Robed in dignity at the court gate, his upright words ever opened wider.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨危致命，盡其心禮。
manualTranslations.literal: Facing peril he gave his life; he exhausted his heart's ritual.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Facing peril he gave his life, fulfilling his heart's duty to the end.

manualTranslations.zh: 堂堂孔明，基宇宏邈。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand, grand Kongming—foundation and structure vast and far.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Zhuge Liang—his foundation and structure were vast and far-reaching.

manualTranslations.zh: 器同生靈，獨稟先覺。
manualTranslations.literal: His vessel matched living spirits; alone he received prior awakening.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His capacity matched the living masses; alone he received prior awakening.

manualTranslations.zh: 標榜風流，遠明管樂。
manualTranslations.literal: He set up elegance as a banner; from afar he illumined Guan and Yue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He held up elegance as his banner; from afar he illumined Guan Zhong and Yue Yi.

manualTranslations.zh: 初九龍盤，雅志彌確。
manualTranslations.literal: At first the nine dragons coiled; his elegant ambition grew ever more sure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first the dragon coiled on the ninth day; his noble ambition grew ever firmer.

manualTranslations.zh: 百六道喪，干戈迭用。
manualTranslations.literal: The hundred six ways were lost; shields and spears were used in turn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The hundred ways were lost; arms were taken up in turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟非命世，孰掃雰雺！
manualTranslations.literal: If not one fated for the age, who could sweep the murky haze!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If not a man fated for the age, who could sweep away the murky haze!

manualTranslations.zh: 宗子思甯，薄言解控。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial scion thought of peace; in brief words he released control.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei thought of peace; in few words he loosened restraint.

manualTranslations.zh: 釋褐中林，郁為時棟。
manualTranslations.literal: Leaving plain cloth in the central grove, he flourished as the age's pillar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Leaving common dress in the central grove, he flourished as the pillar of the age.

manualTranslations.zh: 士元弘長，雅性內融。
manualTranslations.literal: Shiyuan was broad and long; elegant nature inwardly fused.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pang Tong was broad and far-reaching; his refined nature fused within.

manualTranslations.zh: 崇善愛物，觀始知終。
manualTranslations.literal: He honored goodness and loved things; viewing the start he knew the end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He honored goodness and cherished things; seeing the beginning, he knew the end.

manualTranslations.zh: 喪亂備矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Disorder and chaos were complete.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Disorder and chaos were complete.

manualTranslations.zh: 勝塗未隆。
manualTranslations.literal: The path to victory was not yet raised.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The road to victory was not yet raised.

manualTranslations.zh: 先生標之，振起清風。
manualTranslations.literal: The Master marked it out and roused a clear wind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Master Xu marked the way and roused a clear wind.

manualTranslations.zh: 綢繆哲後，無妄惟時。
manualTranslations.literal: He was careful toward the wise successor; without rashness, only with the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was careful toward the wise heir; without rashness, only as the time required.

manualTranslations.zh: 夙夜匪懈，義在緝熙。
manualTranslations.literal: From early night he was not slack; righteousness lay in gathering splendor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From early to late he did not slacken; his duty lay in gathering splendor.

manualTranslations.zh: 三略既陳，霸業已基。
manualTranslations.literal: The three strategies were already set forth; the hegemonic enterprise already had its base.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The three strategies were set forth; the hegemonic enterprise already had its foundation.

manualTranslations.zh: 公琰殖根，不忘中正。
manualTranslations.literal: Gongyan planted his root, not forgetting central correctness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fei Yi planted his root, never forgetting central correctness.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈曰模擬，實在雅性。
manualTranslations.literal: How could one say it was imitation? It truly lay in elegant nature.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This was no mere imitation; it truly lay in his refined nature.

manualTranslations.zh: 亦既羈勒，負荷時命。
manualTranslations.literal: Already bridled and reined, he bore the burden of the age's mandate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Already bridled to office, he bore the burden of the age's mandate.

manualTranslations.zh: 推賢恭己，久而可敬。
manualTranslations.literal: He pushed forward the worthy and was respectful to himself; over time he became worthy of reverence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He promoted the worthy and was humble before others; in time he won deep respect.

manualTranslations.zh: 公衡沖達，秉志淵塞。
manualTranslations.literal: Gongheng was even and penetrating; he held his aim deep and blocked.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi was even and penetrating; he held his resolve deep and firm.

manualTranslations.zh: 媚茲一人，臨難不惑。
manualTranslations.literal: He was gracious to this one man; facing hardship he was not confused.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He honored his sovereign; facing hardship he was not confused.

manualTranslations.zh: 疇昔不造，假翮鄰國。
manualTranslations.literal: In former days he did not succeed; he borrowed wings in a neighboring state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In former days he did not succeed; he borrowed wings in a neighboring state.

manualTranslations.zh: 進能徽音，退不失德。
manualTranslations.literal: Advancing he could send forth fine repute; withdrawing he did not lose virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Advancing he could send forth fine repute; withdrawing he did not lose virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 六合紛紜，人心將變。
manualTranslations.literal: The six directions were tangled and confused; men's hearts were about to change.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The six directions were in turmoil; men's hearts were about to change.

manualTranslations.zh: 鳥擇高梧，臣須顧眄。
manualTranslations.literal: Birds choose high parasol trees; ministers must look back and regard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Birds choose tall parasol trees; ministers must look about with care.

manualTranslations.zh: 公瑾英達，朗心獨見。
manualTranslations.literal: Gongjin was heroic and penetrating; bright of heart, he saw alone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu was heroic and penetrating; bright of heart, he saw alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 披草求君，定交一面。
manualTranslations.literal: Parting the grass he sought his lord; he fixed friendship in a single meeting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Parting the grass he sought his lord; he sealed friendship in a single meeting.

manualTranslations.zh: 桓桓魏武，外托霸跡。
manualTranslations.literal: Mighty, mighty Wei Wu outwardly relied on hegemonic tracks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mighty Cao Cao outwardly relied on the path of hegemony.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓卓若人，曜奇赤壁。
manualTranslations.literal: Outstanding, such a man—his wonder blazed at Red Cliffs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Outstanding such a man—his wonder blazed at Red Cliffs.

manualTranslations.zh: 三光參分，宇宙暫隔。
manualTranslations.literal: The three lights were divided threefold; the universe for a time was parted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The three luminaries were divided threefold; for a time the universe was parted.

manualTranslations.zh: 子布擅名，遭世方擾。
manualTranslations.literal: Zibu monopolized fame; he met an age just in turmoil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao won great renown; he met an age still in turmoil.

manualTranslations.zh: 撫翼桑梓，息肩江表。
manualTranslations.literal: He soothed wings in his native mulberry land; he rested shoulders beyond the river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He spread his wings in his homeland; he rested his shoulders south of the Yangzi.

manualTranslations.zh: 王略威夷，吳魏同寶。
manualTranslations.literal: The king's strategy made might level; Wu and Wei shared the same treasure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The royal strategy leveled threats; Wu and Wei held a shared treasure.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂贊宏謨，匡此霸道。
manualTranslations.literal: Then he praised the great design and rectified this hegemonic Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then he aided the great design and upheld this hegemonic course.

manualTranslations.zh: 桓王之薨，大業未純。
manualTranslations.literal: When Lord Huan died, the great enterprise was not yet pure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce died, the great enterprise was not yet complete.

manualTranslations.zh: 把臂托孤，惟賢與親。
manualTranslations.literal: Clasping arms he entrusted the orphan—only the worthy and the kin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Clasping arms he entrusted the orphan—only the worthy and the kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 轟哭止哀，臨難忘身。
manualTranslations.literal: With a great cry he stopped mourning; facing hardship he forgot himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With a great cry he stopped the mourning; facing hardship he forgot himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 成此南面，實由老臣。
manualTranslations.literal: To accomplish this facing south truly came through the old minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To accomplish this facing south truly came through the old minister.

manualTranslations.zh: 才為世生，世亦須才。
manualTranslations.literal: Talent is born for the age; the age also needs talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Talent is born for the age; the age also needs talent.

manualTranslations.zh: 得而能任，貴在無猜。
manualTranslations.literal: To obtain and be able to employ—what is precious lies in being without suspicion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To gain talent and employ it—what matters is freedom from suspicion.

manualTranslations.zh: 昂昂子敬，拔跡草萊。
manualTranslations.literal: High-lifting, Zijing—he pulled his tracks from grass and weeds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Uplifted Lu Su rose from the common fields.

manualTranslations.zh: 荷簷吐奇，乃構雲臺。
manualTranslations.literal: Bearing the eaves he spat forth wonder; thus he built the Cloud Terrace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bearing the roofbeam he brought forth wonders; thus he built the Cloud Terrace.

manualTranslations.zh: 子瑜都長，體性純懿。
manualTranslations.literal: Ziyu was capital chief; his substance and nature pure and fine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin was chief of the capital; his character was pure and fine.

manualTranslations.zh: 諫而不犯，正而不毅。
manualTranslations.literal: In remonstrance he did not offend; upright yet not harsh.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In remonstrance he gave no offense; upright yet not harsh.

manualTranslations.zh: 將命公庭，退忘私位。
manualTranslations.literal: Bearing mandate in the public court, in withdrawal he forgot private position.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bearing mandate in the public court, in private he forgot personal rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈無鶺鴒，固慎名器。
manualTranslations.literal: Were there not wagtail birds? He firmly was careful of name and vessel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though kin were near as wagtails, he was careful of rank and title.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯言謇謇，以道佐世。
manualTranslations.literal: Boyan was blunt and blunt; with the Way he aided the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Xun was forthright and firm; with the Way he aided the age.

manualTranslations.zh: 出能勤功，入亦獻替。
manualTranslations.literal: Going out he could toil in merit; entering he also offered correction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Going forth he labored in service; returning he offered correction.

manualTranslations.zh: 謀寧社稷，妥紛挫銳。
manualTranslations.literal: His plans settled the altars of soil and grain; he soothed tangles and blunted sharpness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His plans settled the state; he soothed turmoil and blunted sharpness.

manualTranslations.zh: 正以招疑，忠而獲戾。
manualTranslations.literal: Uprightness thereby drew suspicion; loyalty yet received offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Uprightness drew suspicion; loyalty yet met with blame.

manualTranslations.zh: 元歎邈遠，神和形檢。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuantan was remote and far; spirit harmonious, form restrained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gu Yong was remote and far-reaching; harmonious in spirit, restrained in form.

manualTranslations.zh: 如彼白珪，質無塵點。
manualTranslations.literal: Like that white jade tablet—substance without a speck of dust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Like a white jade tablet—his substance bore no speck of dust.

manualTranslations.zh: 立行以恆，匡主以漸。
manualTranslations.literal: He established conduct through constancy; he rectified his lord through gradualness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He established conduct through constancy; he corrected his lord by degrees.

manualTranslations.zh: 清不增潔，濁不加染。
manualTranslations.literal: In purity he did not add cleanliness; in turbidity he did not add stain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In purity he did not grow cleaner; in foulness he took no stain.

manualTranslations.zh: 仲翔高亮，性不和物。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhongxiang was lofty and bright; by nature he did not harmonize with things.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi was lofty and bright; by nature he did not blend with the crowd.

manualTranslations.zh: 好是不群，折而不屈。
manualTranslations.literal: He loved what was not of the herd; broken yet not bent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He loved what set him apart; broken yet unbent.

manualTranslations.zh: 屢摧逆鱗，直道受黜。
manualTranslations.literal: Repeatedly he crushed the reverse scales; the straight Way received dismissal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again and again he touched the dragon's scales; the straight path brought dismissal.

manualTranslations.zh: 歎過孫陽，放同賈屈。
manualTranslations.literal: He sighed passing Sun Yang; released, he was the same as Jia Qu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sighed for lack of a Sun Yang; cast aside, he shared Jia Yi's fate.

manualTranslations.zh: 莘莘眾賢，千載一遇。
manualTranslations.literal: Numerous, numerous—the host of worthies; a thousand years bring one meeting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Numerous worthies all—once in a thousand years such a meeting.

manualTranslations.zh: 整轡高衢，驤首天路。
manualTranslations.literal: They adjusted reins on the high thoroughfare; they raised heads on heaven's road.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They adjusted reins on the high road; they raised their heads on heaven's path.

manualTranslations.zh: 仰揖玄流，俯弘時務。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking up they bowed to the dark stream; looking down they spread the age's affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking up they bowed to the lofty tradition; looking down they advanced the affairs of the age.

manualTranslations.zh: 名節殊塗，雅致同趣。
manualTranslations.literal: Name and integrity had different paths; elegant aim shared the same bent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Integrity took different paths; elegant purpose shared one aim.

manualTranslations.zh: 日月麗天，瞻之不墜。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun and moon beautify heaven; gazing upon them, they do not fall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun and moon adorn the sky; gazing upon them, they do not fall.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁義在躬，用之不匱。
manualTranslations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness were in their persons; using them, they did not fail.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness were in their persons; employed, they never failed.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚想遐風，載揖載味。
manualTranslations.literal: Still thinking of the far wind, they bow again and savor again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Still I think of that far wind, bowing again and savoring again.

manualTranslations.zh: 後生擊節，懦夫增氣。
manualTranslations.literal: Later generations beat the measure; cowards increase their spirit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later generations beat the measure; even cowards take heart.

sourceRange.text: 泰始五年卒，文集行於世。

context.beforeSource: 後遷散騎常侍，以儒學與太尉荀顗撰定新禮，未施行。
context.afterSource: 弟純。
