sourceRange.text: 初，至與康兄子蕃友善，及將遠適，乃與蕃書敘離，並陳其志曰：昔李叟入秦，及關而歎；梁生適越，登嶽長謠。夫以嘉遁之舉，猶懷戀恨，況乎不得已者哉！惟別之後，離群獨逝，背榮宴，辭倫好，經迥路，造沙漠。雞鳴戒旦，則飄爾晨征；日薄西山，則馬首靡托。尋曆曲阻，則沈思紆結；登高遠眺，則山川攸隔。或乃回風狂厲，白日寢光，徙倚交錯，陵隰相望，徘徊九皋之內，慷慨重阜之顛，進無所由，退無所據，涉澤求蹊，披榛覓路，嘯詠溝渠，良不可度。斯亦行路之艱難，然非吾心之所懼也。至若蘭芷傾頓，桂林移殖，根萌未樹而牙淺弦急，每恐風波潛駭，危機密發，此所以怵惕於長衢也。又北土之性，難以托根，投人夜光，鮮不按劍。今將殖橘柚于玄朔，蒂華藕于修陵，表龍章於裸壤，奏《韶》《武》於聾俗，固難以取貴矣。夫物不我貴則莫之與，莫之與則傷之者至矣。飄颻遠遊之士，托身無人之鄉，總轡遐路，則有前言之難；懸鞍陋宇，則有後慮之戒；朝霞啟暉，則身疲而遄征；太陽戢曜，則情劬而夕惕；肆目平隰，則寥廓而無睹；極聽修原，則掩寂而無聞。籲其悲矣！心傷瘁矣！然後知步驟之士不足為貴也。顧景中原，憤中雲踴，哀物悼世，激情風厲。龍嘯大野，獸睇六合，猛志紛紜，雄心四據。思躡雲梯，橫奮八極，披艱掃穢，蕩海夷嶽，蹴昆侖使西倒，蹋太山令東覆，平滌九區，恢維宇宙，斯吾之鄙願也。時不我與，垂翼遠逝，鋒距靡加，六翮摧屈，自非知命，孰能不憤悒者哉！吾子殖根芳苑，濯秀清流，晞葉華崖，飛藻雲肆，俯據潛龍之渚，仰廕游鳳之林，榮曜眩其前，豔色餌其後，良疇交其左，聲名馳其右，翱翔倫黨之間，弄姿帷房之裹，從容顧眄，綽有餘裕，俯仰吟嘯，自以為得志矣，豈能與吾曹同大丈夫之憂樂哉！去矣嵇生，遠離隔矣！煢煢飄寄，臨沙漠矣！悠悠三千，路難涉矣！攜手之期，邈無日矣！思心彌結，誰云釋矣！無金玉爾音而有遐心。身雖胡越，意存斷金。各敬爾儀，敦履璞沈，繁華流蕩，君子弗欽。臨紙意結，知復何云。

manualTranslations.zh: 初，至與康兄子蕃友善，及將遠適，乃與蕃書敘離，並陳其志曰：昔李叟入秦，及關而歎；
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Zhi was friendly with Kang's elder brother's son Fan; when about to go far away, he then wrote Fan a letter narrating parting and stating his intent, saying: In olden days Old Man Li entered Qin—reaching the pass he sighed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhi had long been close to Ji Fan, nephew of Xi Kang; before departing for distant lands he sent Fan a farewell letter laying bare his heart, beginning: Long ago Laozi entered Qin and sighed at the frontier pass;

manualTranslations.zh: 梁生適越，登嶽長謠。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Sheng went to Yue, climbed the mountain and sang long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang Hong set out for Yue and poured out a long song from the heights.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫以嘉遁之舉，猶懷戀恨，況乎不得已者哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Now as for the act of fine withdrawal, they still cherished fond regret—how much more when one has no choice!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even those who withdraw in noble ease still feel the ache of parting—how much more one who goes against his will!

manualTranslations.zh: 惟別之後，離群獨逝，背榮宴，辭倫好，經迥路，造沙漠。
manualTranslations.literal: Since parting, leaving the flock I go alone, turning my back on honored feasting, bidding farewell to worthy fellowship, traversing winding roads, reaching the desert.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since we parted I have traveled alone, leaving feasts and friends behind, crossing twisting roads until I stand at the desert's edge.

manualTranslations.zh: 雞鳴戒旦，則飄爾晨征；
manualTranslations.literal: At cockcrow warning dawn, then lightly I set out at morning;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At cockcrow I rise and fare forth at dawn;

manualTranslations.zh: 日薄西山，則馬首靡托。
manualTranslations.literal: The sun draws near western mountains, then my horse's head has nowhere to rest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when the sun sinks west, my horse has nowhere to halt.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋曆曲阻，則沈思紆結；
manualTranslations.literal: Soon traversing winding barriers, then deep thought knots and coils;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On winding passes my thoughts knot tight;

manualTranslations.zh: 登高遠眺，則山川攸隔。
manualTranslations.literal: Climbing high and gazing far, then mountains and rivers are sundered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: from lofty vistas mountains and rivers stretch infinitely between us.

manualTranslations.zh: 或乃回風狂厲，白日寢光，徙倚交錯，陵隰相望，徘徊九皋之內，慷慨重阜之顛，進無所由，退無所據，涉澤求蹊，披榛覓路，嘯詠溝渠，良不可度。
manualTranslations.literal: Sometimes whirling wind is fierce and violent, the white sun hides its light; I linger and lean crisscrossing, hills and marshes facing one another; I pace within the nine marshes, pour forth feeling on heavy knolls' crests; advancing there is no path, retreating there is no foothold; crossing swamps seeking tracks, parting brambles seeking roads—whistling and chanting in ditches and channels—truly cannot be crossed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sometimes wild winds howl and daylight dies; I wander lost among hills and bogs, pacing the reedy flats and brooding on high ridges—no way forward, no place to turn back. I wade marshes for a trail, hack through brambles for a road, and whistle verses in muddy channels where none may pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 斯亦行路之艱難，然非吾心之所懼也。
manualTranslations.literal: This too is the hardship of travel on the road—yet it is not what my heart fears.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such are the trials of the road—but they are not what I dread.

manualTranslations.zh: 至若蘭芷傾頓，桂林移殖，根萌未樹而牙淺弦急，每恐風波潛駭，危機密發，此所以怵惕於長衢也。
manualTranslations.literal: As for orchids and angelica overturned, cassia trees transplanted—roots and sprouts not yet set while the bow is shallow-drawn and the string tight—each time I fear hidden shock of wind and waves, peril's moment secretly arising; this is why I am fearful and wary on the long highway.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What I dread is orchid and cassia uprooted and replanted—roots not yet firm while the bow is taut—lest hidden storms strike and danger burst forth without warning. That is why I tremble on this long road.

manualTranslations.zh: 又北土之性，難以托根，投人夜光，鮮不按劍。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the nature of northern soil is hard to take root in; casting a luminous gem before others, few do not lay hand to sword.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The northern lands are hard soil for transplanting; show a luminous pearl to strangers and few will not reach for their swords.

manualTranslations.zh: 今將殖橘柚于玄朔，蒂華藕于修陵，表龍章於裸壤，奏《韶》《武》於聾俗，固難以取貴矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Now I am about to plant orange and pomelo in dark northlands, set lotus stems and flowers on Xiu Mound, display dragon emblems on bare soil, perform "Shao" and "Wu" for deaf custom—truly hard to win esteem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I go to plant oranges in the far north, set lotus on barren hills, display dragon insignia on naked earth, and play the "Shao" and "Wu" hymns to deaf ears—how can such gifts win honor?

manualTranslations.zh: 夫物不我貴則莫之與，莫之與則傷之者至矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Now if things do not prize me then none will join with me; if none join with me then those who wound will arrive in full.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the world does not value you, none will stand with you; and when none stand with you, injury is sure to come.

manualTranslations.zh: 飄颻遠遊之士，托身無人之鄉，總轡遐路，則有前言之難；
manualTranslations.literal: A drifting far-wandering gentleman, lodging his person in a land without men, gathering reins on distant roads—then there is the hardship of words already spoken;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A wanderer adrift in empty country, reins in hand on endless roads, faces the hardship foretold by sages;

manualTranslations.zh: 懸鞍陋宇，則有後慮之戒；
manualTranslations.literal: hanging saddle in a mean dwelling—then there is the warning of later concern;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and stabling his horse in a wretched inn, the warning of troubles yet to come.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝霞啟暉，則身疲而遄征；
manualTranslations.literal: morning rosy clouds open radiance—then the body is weary yet hastens on campaign;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At dawn's first light his weary body presses on;

manualTranslations.zh: 太陽戢曜，則情劬而夕惕；
manualTranslations.literal: the great sun sheathes its brilliance—then feeling is toiled and evening-cautious;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: at sunset his heart labors and he keeps vigil through the night.

manualTranslations.zh: 肆目平隰，則寥廓而無睹；
manualTranslations.literal: releasing the eye over level lowlands—then vast emptiness and nothing seen;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He scans the flat plains and sees only emptiness;

manualTranslations.zh: 極聽修原，則掩寂而無聞。
manualTranslations.literal: listening to the limit on long plains—then muffled silence and nothing heard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he listens across the open steppe and hears only silence.

manualTranslations.zh: 籲其悲矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

manualTranslations.zh: 心傷瘁矣！
manualTranslations.literal: The heart is wounded and worn!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The heart is wounded to exhaustion!

manualTranslations.zh: 然後知步驟之士不足為貴也。
manualTranslations.literal: Only then does one know that gentlemen of measured pace are not worth esteeming.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only then does one see that men content with small steps are no fit measure of worth.

manualTranslations.zh: 顧景中原，憤中雲踴，哀物悼世，激情風厲。
manualTranslations.literal: Turning sight to the central plains, rage within surges like clouds; grieving things and mourning the age, fierce feeling blazes like wind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I look back toward the heartland and rage boils within; grieving for the world, my passion rises fierce as a gale.

manualTranslations.zh: 龍嘯大野，獸睇六合，猛志紛紜，雄心四據。
manualTranslations.literal: A dragon roars across the great wilds, beasts gaze upon the six quarters; fierce intent tangles in profusion, bold heart seizes the four directions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My spirit roars like a dragon across the wilds and surveys the realm; fierce purpose swarms and bold ambition grips all four quarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 思躡雲梯，橫奮八極，披艱掃穢，蕩海夷嶽，蹴昆侖使西倒，蹋太山令東覆，平滌九區，恢維宇宙，斯吾之鄙願也。
manualTranslations.literal: I think to tread the cloud ladder, stride across and strive through the eight extremities, part hardship and sweep defilement, level seas and flatten mountains, kick Kunlun to make it fall westward, tread Mount Tai to make it overturn eastward, level and cleanse the nine regions, restore and sustain the cosmos—this is my humble wish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I dream of climbing heaven's ladder and ranging the eight extremes—cutting through hardship, cleansing corruption, flattening seas and mountains, kicking Kunlun westward and toppling Tai eastward, purging the nine provinces and ordering the universe. That is my humble ambition.

manualTranslations.zh: 時不我與，垂翼遠逝，鋒距靡加，六翮摧屈，自非知命，孰能不憤悒者哉！
manualTranslations.literal: The age does not grant me its time; wings droop as I go far away; talons and spurs cannot be applied, six pinions are broken and bent—if not one who knows fate, who could fail to be angry and depressed!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven's hour is not mine: wings folded, I fly into exile; talons blunted, pinions broken—who but one resigned to fate could bear such bitterness!

manualTranslations.zh: 吾子殖根芳苑，濯秀清流，晞葉華崖，飛藻雲肆，俯據潛龍之渚，仰廕游鳳之林，榮曜眩其前，豔色餌其後，良疇交其左，聲名馳其右，翱翔倫黨之間，弄姿帷房之裹，從容顧眄，綽有餘裕，俯仰吟嘯，自以為得志矣，豈能與吾曹同大丈夫之憂樂哉！
manualTranslations.literal: My lord plants roots in fragrant gardens, washes splendor in clear streams, dries leaves on flowery cliffs, lets ornament fly in cloud's expanse; below he occupies the ford of hidden dragons, above he is shaded by the grove of roaming phoenixes—glory dazzles before him, gorgeous color lures behind him, fine companions meet at his left, fame races at his right; soaring among kindred fellows, displaying grace within curtain chambers, at ease in glance and look, ample in surplus ease, bowing and rising in chant and whistle—he takes himself to have attained his aim—how could he share with men like us a great man's cares and joys!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have rooted yourself in fragrant gardens, bathed in clear streams, flourished on sunny cliffs, and let your talents soar among the clouds. Below lies the dragon's ford; above, the phoenix's grove—glory dazzles before you, beauty tempts behind, fine friends at your left, fame racing at your right. You glide among peers and preen within curtained chambers, serene and at ease, chanting and whistling as though life were complete—how could you share a great man's joys and sorrows with men like us!

manualTranslations.zh: 去矣嵇生，遠離隔矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Gone is Master Ji, far parted and sundered!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Farewell, Xi Kang—how far we are sundered!

manualTranslations.zh: 煢煢飄寄，臨沙漠矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Alone and drifting, lodged, facing the desert!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alone I drift, adrift at the desert's edge!

manualTranslations.zh: 悠悠三千，路難涉矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Vast and long, three thousand—hard the road to cross!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three thousand leagues stretch before me—how hard the road to cross!

manualTranslations.zh: 攜手之期，邈無日矣！
manualTranslations.literal: The time of joined hands—remote, no day!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The day we might join hands again seems endlessly far!

manualTranslations.zh: 思心彌結，誰云釋矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Thinking heart ever more bound—who says it is released!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My thoughts bind ever tighter—who says they can be loosed!

manualTranslations.zh: 無金玉爾音而有遐心。
manualTranslations.literal: Without gold and jade is your message, yet there is a far-reaching heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though no precious word comes from you, my heart reaches far to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 身雖胡越，意存斷金。
manualTranslations.literal: Though body is Hu and Yue apart, intent remains severing-gold.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though our bodies stand as far apart as north and south, our bond remains unbreakable as sworn gold.

manualTranslations.zh: 各敬爾儀，敦履璞沈，繁華流蕩，君子弗欽。
manualTranslations.literal: Each respect your deportment, earnestly tread submerged uncut jade—flowery splendor drifting in dissipation, the gentleman does not esteem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guard your conduct, keep your uncut jade hidden in depth; the gentleman does not prize gaudy dissipation.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨紙意結，知復何云。
manualTranslations.literal: Facing the paper, intent knots—knowing again what to say.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Facing this page my thoughts knot tight—what more is there to say?

context.beforeSource: 年七十七卒，所著文章行於世。
context.afterSource: 顧愷之，字長康，晉陵無錫人也。

sourceRange.text: 幼好刑名之學，深抑虛浮之士，嘗著《學箴》，稱：《老子》云：「絕仁棄義，家復孝慈。」豈仁義之道絕，然後李慈乃生哉？蓋患乎情仁義者寡而利仁義者眾也。道德喪而仁義彰，仁義彰而名利作，禮教之弊，直在茲也。先王以道德之不行，故以仁義化之，行仁義之不篤，故以禮律檢之；檢之彌繁，而偽亦愈廣，老莊是乃明無為之益，塞爭欲之門。夫極靈智之妙、總會通之和者，莫尚乎聖人。革一代之弘制，垂千載之遺風，則非聖不立。然則聖人之在世，吐言則為訓辭，蒞事則為物軌，運通則與時隆，理喪則與世弊矣。是以大為之論以標其旨。物必有宗，事必有主，寄責于聖人而遺累乎陳跡也。故化之以絕聖棄智，鎮之以無名之樸。聖教救其末，老莊明其本，本末之塗殊而為教一也。人之迷也，其日久矣！見形者眾，及道者鮮，不覿千仞之門而遂適物之跡，逐跡逾篤，離本逾遠，遂使華端與薄俗俱興，妙緒與淳風並絕，所以聖人長潛而跡未嘗滅矣。懼後進惑其如此，將越禮棄學而希無為之風，見義教之殺而不觀其隆矣，略言所懷，以補其闕。引道家之弘旨，會世教之適當，義之違本，言不流放，庶以祛困蒙之蔽，悟一往之惑乎！其辭曰：芒芒太初，悠悠鴻荒，蚩蚩萬類，與道兼忘。聖跡未顯，賢名不彰，怡此鼓腹，率我倡狂。資生既廣，群塗思通，暗實師明，匪予求蒙，遺己濟物而天下為公。大庭唱基，義農宏贊，六位元時成，離暉大觀，澤洽雨濡，化流風散，比屋同塵而人罔僭亂。爰暨中古，哲王胥承，質文代作，禮統迭興，事藉用以繁，化因阻而凝，動非性擾，靜豈神澄！名之攸彰，道之攸廢，乃損所隆，乃崇所替，刑作由於德衰，三辟興乎叔世，既敦既誘，乃矯乃厲。敦亦既備，矯亦既深，雕琢生文，抑揚成音，群能騁技，眾巧竭心，野無陸馬，山無散林。風罔不動，化罔不移，人之失德，反正作奇。乃放欲以越禮，不知希競之為病，違彼夷塗而遵此險徑。狡兔陵岡，游魚遁川，至賾深妙，大象幽玄，棄餌收罝而責功蹄筌，先統喪歸而寄旨忘言。政異征辭，拔本塞源，遁跡永日，尋響窮年，刻意離性而失其自然。世有險夷，運有通圮，損益適時，升降惟理。道不可以一日廢，亦不可以一朝擬，禮不可以千載制，亦不可以當年止。非仁無以長物，非義無以齊恥，仁義固不可遠，去其害仁義者而己。力行猶懼不逮，希企邈以遠矣。室有善言，應在千里，況乎行止復禮克己。風人司箴，敬貽君子。

manualTranslations.zh: 幼好刑名之學，深抑虛浮之士，嘗著《學箴》，稱：《老子》云：「絕仁棄義，家復孝慈。」
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he loved the learning of punishment and names; he deeply suppressed empty floating gentlemen—once he composed "Admonition on Learning," saying: The Laozi says: "Cut off benevolence, discard righteousness, and the family again has filial piety and kindness."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From youth he studied legalist doctrine and scorned fashionable emptiness; in his "Admonition on Learning" he writes: Laozi says, "Abandon benevolence and discard righteousness, and the household will again know filial piety and kindness."

manualTranslations.zh: 豈仁義之道絕，然後李慈乃生哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Could it be that only when the Way of benevolence and righteousness is cut off does filial kindness then arise?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Does filial kindness arise only after benevolence and righteousness have been abolished?

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋患乎情仁義者寡而利仁義者眾也。
manualTranslations.literal: It is rather that those who feel benevolence and righteousness are few, while those who profit from benevolence and righteousness are many.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The trouble is that few feel benevolence and righteousness in their hearts, while many profit from them.

manualTranslations.zh: 道德喪而仁義彰，仁義彰而名利作，禮教之弊，直在茲也。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Way and virtue are lost, benevolence and righteousness are displayed; when benevolence and righteousness are displayed, fame and profit arise—the defect of ritual teaching lies directly in this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Way and virtue decline, benevolence and righteousness are proclaimed; when those are proclaimed, fame and profit follow—the flaw of ritual teaching lies here.

manualTranslations.zh: 先王以道德之不行，故以仁義化之，行仁義之不篤，故以禮律檢之；
manualTranslations.literal: Former kings, because the Way and virtue did not prevail, therefore used benevolence and righteousness to transform; because practicing benevolence and righteousness was not sincere, therefore used ritual and law to examine;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Way and virtue failed to prevail, the ancient kings taught through benevolence and righteousness; when practice grew insincere, they restrained conduct with ritual and law;

manualTranslations.zh: 檢之彌繁，而偽亦愈廣，老莊是乃明無為之益，塞爭欲之門。
manualTranslations.literal: the more examination, the broader also hypocrisy—Laozi and Zhuangzi therefore clarified the benefit of non-action and blocked the gate of contentious desire.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: yet the more rules multiplied, the wider hypocrisy spread—hence Laozi and Zhuangzi showed the good of non-action and closed the gate of strife and craving.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫極靈智之妙、總會通之和者，莫尚乎聖人。
manualTranslations.literal: Now one who reaches the wonder of spiritual intelligence and gathers the harmony of comprehensive penetration—none is loftier than the sage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: None surpasses the sage in reaching the heights of wisdom and gathering the harmony of universal truth.

manualTranslations.zh: 革一代之弘制，垂千載之遺風，則非聖不立。
manualTranslations.literal: Reforming a generation's great institutions, handing down a thousand years' legacy-wind—then without the sage it is not established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Great institutions are not reformed nor enduring customs handed down except through the sage.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則聖人之在世，吐言則為訓辭，蒞事則為物軌，運通則與時隆，理喪則與世弊矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus when the sage is in the world, uttering words then becomes instructive diction, presiding over affairs then becomes the track of things; when fortune is penetrating he rises with the age, when principle is lost he declines with the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the sage lives among men, his words become teaching and his conduct a model for all things; in prosperous times he rises with the age, and when principle fails he shares the world's decline.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以大為之論以標其旨。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore I greatly compose this discourse to mark its aim.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore I set forth this broad argument to make its purpose clear.

manualTranslations.zh: 物必有宗，事必有主，寄責于聖人而遺累乎陳跡也。
manualTranslations.literal: Things must have their origin, affairs must have their master—entrust responsibility to the sage and leave the burden upon stale traces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All things have their root and all affairs their master; fix responsibility on the sage and leave stale forms behind.

manualTranslations.zh: 故化之以絕聖棄智，鎮之以無名之樸。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore transform them by cutting off sagehood and discarding wisdom, stabilize them by the nameless uncarved block.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus teach by setting aside false sagehood and cleverness, and steady the age with the nameless uncarved block.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖教救其末，老莊明其本，本末之塗殊而為教一也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sage teaching rescues the branch-tips; Laozi and Zhuangzi clarify the root—the paths of root and branch differ, yet as teaching they are one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Confucian teaching remedies the branches; Laozi and Zhuangzi illuminate the root—the paths differ, yet the teaching is one.

manualTranslations.zh: 人之迷也，其日久矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Men's delusion—its days have been long!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men have wandered in delusion for ages!

manualTranslations.zh: 見形者眾，及道者鮮，不覿千仞之門而遂適物之跡，逐跡逾篤，離本逾遠，遂使華端與薄俗俱興，妙緒與淳風並絕，所以聖人長潛而跡未嘗滅矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who see form are many, those who reach the Way are few; not beholding the thousand-ren gate yet thereupon adapting to things' traces—chasing traces ever more ardent, departing from the root ever farther—thus causing flowery branch-tips and shallow custom to rise together, subtle threads and pure wind to perish together; therefore the sage long remains hidden yet his traces have never been extinguished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many see only appearances; few attain the Way. Ignoring the lofty gate, they chase outward traces ever more eagerly and drift ever farther from the root—so ornament and vulgarity flourish together while subtle truth and pure custom die together. That is why the sage often withdraws, yet his traces are never lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 懼後進惑其如此，將越禮棄學而希無為之風，見義教之殺而不觀其隆矣，略言所懷，以補其闕。
manualTranslations.literal: Fearing that later comers will be deluded in this way, they will overstep ritual and abandon learning to hope for the wind of non-action, seeing righteous teaching as stifling without observing its elevation—I briefly state what I harbor to mend its lack.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lest later students be misled into casting off ritual and study to chase idle non-action, seeing moral teaching as mere constraint without noting its uplifting power, I briefly set down my thoughts to fill what is lacking.

manualTranslations.zh: 引道家之弘旨，會世教之適當，義之違本，言不流放，庶以祛困蒙之蔽，悟一往之惑乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Drawing the broad aim of the Daoist school, meeting the worldly teaching's fitness—meaning not departing from the root, words not flowing unrestrained—perhaps thereby to remove the obstruction of trapped ignorance and awaken the delusion of one-sided going!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I draw on the great aim of Daoism and align it with what worldly teaching requires—keeping meaning true to the root and language from wandering free—in hope of lifting the blinders of confusion and awakening those trapped in one-sided views!

manualTranslations.zh: 其辭曰：芒芒太初，悠悠鴻荒，蚩蚩萬類，與道兼忘。
manualTranslations.literal: Its words say: Vast vast primal beginning, far far great wilds, simple simple ten thousand kinds, with the Way together forgotten.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The text runs: In vast primordial chaos, in boundless antiquity, all creatures lived in simple innocence and forgot even the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖跡未顯，賢名不彰，怡此鼓腹，率我倡狂。
manualTranslations.literal: Sage traces not yet displayed, worthy names not yet shown—content with this drum-belly, leading us to sing wildly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No sage's traces yet appeared, no worthy name was known—bellies full, hearts content, all sang in untamed ease.

manualTranslations.zh: 資生既廣，群塗思通，暗實師明，匪予求蒙，遺己濟物而天下為公。
manualTranslations.literal: Sustaining life already broad, the many paths thought to penetrate; the dark in truth took the bright as teacher—not I seeking obscurity—forgetting self to aid things and all under heaven was common.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As livelihoods broadened, every path sought mastery; the benighted took the enlightened as teacher—not to seek ignorance, but to forget self, aid others, and make the realm common to all.

manualTranslations.zh: 大庭唱基，義農宏贊，六位元時成，離暉大觀，澤洽雨濡，化流風散，比屋同塵而人罔僭亂。
manualTranslations.literal: Great Court sang the foundation, righteous farmers broadly praised; the six positions at the primal time were completed, Li radiance great observation—favor soaking like rain, transformation flowing like wind's dispersal—house by house same dust and men had no usurpation and disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Great Sovereign laid the foundation; the righteous farmers exalted his reign. The six offices were set, the great radiance shone forth; grace soaked like rain, transformation spread like wind, every household shared one dust, and none usurped or rebelled.

manualTranslations.zh: 爰暨中古，哲王胥承，質文代作，禮統迭興，事藉用以繁，化因阻而凝，動非性擾，靜豈神澄！
manualTranslations.literal: Then reaching middle antiquity, wise kings all inherited; substance and ornament alternately arose, ritual systems repeatedly rose; affairs relied on use and became complex, transformation because of obstruction became congealed—movement was not nature disturbed, stillness how could spirit be clear!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then in middle antiquity sage kings succeeded one another; culture and ornament alternated, ritual systems rose in turn. Affairs grew complex through utility, transformation stiffened through obstruction—movement no longer sprang from nature, stillness no longer cleared the spirit!

manualTranslations.zh: 名之攸彰，道之攸廢，乃損所隆，乃崇所替，刑作由於德衰，三辟興乎叔世，既敦既誘，乃矯乃厲。
manualTranslations.literal: Where names were displayed, there the Way was abandoned—then reducing what was exalted, then honoring what was replaced; punishments arose from virtue's decline, three penal codes rose in the declining age—both earnest instruction and both correction and severity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As names were exalted, the Way was cast aside—what had been honored was cut back, what had been discarded was raised up. Punishments arose as virtue waned; three penal codes appeared in a decadent age—through teaching and warning, correction and severity.

manualTranslations.zh: 敦亦既備，矯亦既深，雕琢生文，抑揚成音，群能騁技，眾巧竭心，野無陸馬，山無散林。
manualTranslations.literal: Earnest instruction also already complete, correction also already deep—carving and polishing produced ornament, restraint and release made tones; the many talents displayed skill, the crowd of craft exhausted mind; fields had no land-roaming horses, mountains had no scattered groves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Instruction was complete, correction ran deep—carving produced ornament, modulation shaped music; talents vied in skill, ingenuity exhausted every mind; no horse roamed the plain, no tree stood scattered on the hill.

manualTranslations.zh: 風罔不動，化罔不移，人之失德，反正作奇。
manualTranslations.literal: Wind none did not move, transformation none did not shift—men lost virtue, turned from the correct and made the strange.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No wind stirred, no change moved—yet men lost virtue, turned from the straight path, and pursued the bizarre.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃放欲以越禮，不知希競之為病，違彼夷塗而遵此險徑。
manualTranslations.literal: Then they released desire to overstep ritual, not knowing that hoping to compete is sickness—violating that level path and following this perilous track.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They indulged desire to breach ritual, never seeing that craving rivalry is a sickness—leaving the level road for this treacherous path.

manualTranslations.zh: 狡兔陵岡，游魚遁川，至賾深妙，大象幽玄，棄餌收罝而責功蹄筌，先統喪歸而寄旨忘言。
manualTranslations.literal: Crafty hare mounts the hillock, roaming fish escapes the stream—the utmost subtlety deep and wondrous, the great image dark and abstruse; casting bait and gathering nets yet demanding achievement of hoof and fish-trap, first the lineage lost in return yet entrusting aim to forgetting words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The crafty hare climbs the hill, the roaming fish flees the stream—the deepest mystery is profound, the great image dark and abstruse. They cast aside bait and nets yet demand results like hoofprints and fish-traps; having lost the original unity, they rest their meaning on wordless teaching.

manualTranslations.zh: 政異征辭，拔本塞源，遁跡永日，尋響窮年，刻意離性而失其自然。
manualTranslations.literal: Governance differed and proof-words arose; uprooting the root and blocking the source, hiding traces for endless days, seeking echoes for exhausted years—deliberately departing from nature and losing its spontaneity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Policies diverged and disputations multiplied—uprooting the source, blocking the spring, hiding away day after day, chasing echoes year after year—forcing nature aside and losing what is spontaneous.

manualTranslations.zh: 世有險夷，運有通圮，損益適時，升降惟理。
manualTranslations.literal: The age has peril and ease, fortune has penetration and ruin—increase and decrease fit the time, rising and falling follow principle alone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ages bring peril and ease, fortune brings rise and fall—increase and decrease must suit the time, ascent and decline follow reason alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 道不可以一日廢，亦不可以一朝擬，禮不可以千載制，亦不可以當年止。
manualTranslations.literal: The Way cannot for one day be abandoned, nor can it in one morning be drafted; ritual cannot for a thousand years be fixed, nor can it in the present year be halted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Way may not be abandoned for a single day, nor seized in a single morning; ritual may not be fixed for a thousand years, nor halted in the present year.

manualTranslations.zh: 非仁無以長物，非義無以齊恥，仁義固不可遠，去其害仁義者而己。
manualTranslations.literal: Without benevolence there is no means to nurture things, without righteousness there is no means to align shame—benevolence and righteousness truly cannot be kept far; remove only those who harm benevolence and righteousness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without benevolence nothing can flourish; without righteousness shame cannot be ordered. Benevolence and righteousness must not be cast away—only remove what harms them.

manualTranslations.zh: 力行猶懼不逮，希企邈以遠矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Forceful practice still fears not reaching—hoping to attain the remote is far indeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even strenuous effort fears falling short; to hope for the distant ideal is harder still.

manualTranslations.zh: 室有善言，應在千里，況乎行止復禮克己。
manualTranslations.literal: When the house has good words, response should be at a thousand li—how much more conduct and stopping returning to ritual and restraining self.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Good words in one's household should resound a thousand leagues away—how much more when conduct and restraint return to ritual and self-mastery.

manualTranslations.zh: 風人司箴，敬貽君子。
manualTranslations.literal: The wind-man oversees admonition—respectfully bequeathed to the gentleman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The poet charged with admonition respectfully offers this to gentlemen.

localRange.text: 詳觀往誥，逖聽前聞，階緣外戚以致顯榮者，其所由來尚矣。而多至禍敗，鮮克令終者，何哉？豈不由祿以恩升，位非德舉；識慚明悊。材謝經通；假椒房之寵靈，總軍國之樞要。或威權震主，或勢力傾朝；居安而不慮危，務進而不知退；驕奢既至，釁隙隨之者乎！是以呂霍之家，誅夷于西漢，梁鄧之族，剿絕於東都，其餘干紀亂常、害時蠹政者，不可勝載。至若樊靡卿之父子，竇廣國之弟兄，陰興之守約戒奢，史丹之掩惡揚善，斯並后族之所美者也。由此觀之，干時縱溢者必以凶終，守道謙沖者永保貞吉，古人所謂禍福無門，惟人所召，此非其效歟！逮于晉難，始自宮掖。楊駿藉武帝之寵私，叨竊非據，賈謐乘惠皇之蒙昧，成此厲階，遂使悼后遇雲林之災，湣懷濫湖城之酷。天人道盡，喪亂弘多，宗廟以之顛覆，黎庶於焉殄瘁。《詩》云：「赫赫宗周，褒姒滅之。其此之謂也。爰及江左，未改覆車。庾亮世族羽儀，王恭高門領袖，既而職兼出納，任切股肱。孝伯竟以亡身，元規幾于敗國，豈不哀哉！若褚季野之畏避朝權，王叔仁之固求出鎮，用能全身遠害，有可稱焉。賈充、楊駿、庾亮、王獻之、王恭等已入列傳，其餘既敘其成敗，以為《外戚篇》云。

sourceRange.text: 胤，敬后弟也。初拜散騎常侍，遷步兵校尉。太寧末，追贈豫官，以胤襲侯爵，轉右衛將軍。與南頓王宗俱為明帝所昵，並典禁兵。及帝不豫，宗以陰謀發覺，事連胤，帝隱忍不問，徙胤為宗正卿，加散騎常侍。咸和二年，宗伏誅，左遷胤為桂陽太守，秩中二千石。頻徙琅邪、盧陵太守。咸康元年卒，追贈衛將軍，加散騎常侍。子洪襲爵。

manualTranslations.zh: 胤，敬后弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yin was the younger brother of Empress Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu Yin was a younger brother of Empress Yuanjing.

manualTranslations.zh: 初拜散騎常侍，遷步兵校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he was appointed Regular Cavalier Attendant and was transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was first named Regular Cavalier Attendant, then Commandant of Footsoldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 太寧末，追贈豫官，以胤襲侯爵，轉右衛將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Near the end of Taining, the honors of Yu were posthumously conferred so that Yin could inherit the marquisate; he was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Late in Taining the court posthumously conferred his father Yu Yu’s honors so Yin could inherit the marquisate, then named him General of the Right Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 與南頓王宗俱為明帝所昵，並典禁兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Together with Prince Sima Zong of Nandun he was both favored by Emperor Ming and jointly held command of the palace guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He and Prince Sima Zong of Nandun were both favorites of Emperor Ming and together commanded the palace guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 及帝不豫，宗以陰謀發覺，事連胤，帝隱忍不問，徙胤為宗正卿，加散騎常侍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, Zong’s secret plot was discovered and the affair implicated Yin; the emperor concealed his anger and did not inquire, transferring Yin to Director of the Imperial Clan and adding Regular Cavalier Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Zong’s conspiracy was uncovered and Yin was implicated; the emperor held his peace, moved Yin to Director of the Imperial Clan, and added Regular Cavalier Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸和二年，宗伏誅，左遷胤為桂陽太守，秩中二千石。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Xianhe, Zong was executed; Yin was demoted to Administrator of Guiyang with salary of two thousand shi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 327 Zong was executed and Yin was demoted to Administrator of Guiyang at the salary grade of two thousand shi.

manualTranslations.zh: 頻徙琅邪、盧陵太守。
manualTranslations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred as Administrator of Langye and Luling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was later shifted to the administrations of Langye and Luling.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸康元年卒，追贈衛將軍，加散騎常侍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Xiankang he died; he was posthumously awarded General of the Guard and added as Regular Cavalier Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in 335 and was posthumously named General of the Guard with the added title of Regular Cavalier Attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 子洪襲爵。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Hong inherited the title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Yu Hong inherited the marquisate.

sourceRange.text: 何准，字幼道，穆章皇后父也。高尚寡欲，弱冠知名，州府交辟，並不就。兄充為驃騎將軍，勸其令仕，准曰：「第五之名何滅驃騎？」准兄弟中第五，故有此言。充居宰輔之重，權傾一時，而准散帶衡門，不及人事，唯誦佛經，修營塔廟而已。徵拜散騎郎，不起。年四十七卒。昇平元年，追贈金紫光祿大夫，封晉興縣侯。子惔以父素行高潔，表讓不受。三子：放、惔、澄。放繼充。

manualTranslations.zh: 何准，字幼道，穆章皇后父也。
manualTranslations.literal: He Zhun, styled Youdao, was the father of Empress Muzhang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Zhun, courtesy name Youdao, was the father of Empress Muzhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 高尚寡欲，弱冠知名，州府交辟，並不就。
manualTranslations.literal: Lofty and few in desires, famed at the capping age, commanderies and prefectures repeatedly summoned him, and he accepted none.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: High-minded and detached, he was celebrated from youth; repeated summons from local authorities went unanswered.

manualTranslations.zh: 兄充為驃騎將軍，勸其令仕，准曰：「第五之名何滅驃騎？」
manualTranslations.literal: His elder brother Chong was General Who Gallops as if Flying and urged him to take office; Zhun said: "How does the name of the fifth compare unfavorably to General Who Gallops as if Flying?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His elder brother He Chong, General Who Gallops as if Flying, urged him to serve; He Zhun replied, "How is the fifth son’s name any less than General Who Gallops as if Flying?"

manualTranslations.zh: 准兄弟中第五，故有此言。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhun was the fifth among the brothers, hence this saying.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhun was the fifth of the brothers, which explains the remark.

manualTranslations.zh: 充居宰輔之重，權傾一時，而准散帶衡門，不及人事，唯誦佛經，修營塔廟而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong held the weight of chief minister and his power tilted the age, while Zhun wore an official sash behind a plain gate, did not attend to human affairs, and only recited Buddhist sutras and built and maintained pagodas and temples.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While He Chong wielded chief-ministerial power, He Zhun kept his rank but lived behind a humble gate, ignored public affairs, and devoted himself to Buddhist scripture and temple building.

manualTranslations.zh: 徵拜散騎郎，不起。
manualTranslations.literal: Summoned and appointed Cavalier Attendant, he did not rise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Cavalier Attendant but would not serve.

manualTranslations.zh: 年四十七卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He died at age forty-seven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at forty-seven.

manualTranslations.zh: 昇平元年，追贈金紫光祿大夫，封晉興縣侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Shengping he was posthumously awarded Household Grandee with Golden Girdle and Purple Trappings and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinxing County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 357 he was posthumously named Household Grandee with Golden Girdle and Purple Trappings and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinxing County.

manualTranslations.zh: 子惔以父素行高潔，表讓不受。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Tan, on account of his father’s plain conduct and lofty purity, memorialized to decline and did not accept.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son He Tan, citing his father’s austere virtue, memorialized to decline the honors and did not accept them.

manualTranslations.zh: 三子：放、惔、澄。
manualTranslations.literal: Three sons: Fang, Tan, and Cheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had three sons: He Fang, He Tan, and He Cheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 放繼充。
manualTranslations.literal: Fang succeeded Chong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Fang succeeded He Chong as head of the lineage.

localRange.text: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；在盈斯害，惟神之常道。古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。

sourceRange.text: 侍御史西河郭欽上疏曰：戎狄強獷，曆古爲患。魏初人寡，西北諸郡皆爲戎居。今雖服從，若百年之後有風塵之警，胡騎自平陽、上黨不三日而至孟津，北地、西河、太原、馮翊、安定、上郡盡爲狄庭矣。宜及平吳之威，謀臣猛將之略，出北地、西河、安定，復上郡，實馮翊，於平陽已北諸縣募取死罪，徙三河、三魏見士四萬家以充之。裔不亂華，漸徙平陽、弘農、魏郡、京兆、上党雜胡，峻四夷出入之防，明先王荒服之制，萬世之長策也。

sourceRange.text: 勒之居襄國，署為魏郡太守，鎮鄴三台，後封繁陽侯。勒即大單于、趙王位，署為單于元輔、都督禁衛諸軍事，遷侍中、開府，進封中山公。及勒僭號，授太尉、守尚書令，進封為王，邑萬戶。季龍自以勳高一時，謂勒即位之後，大單于必在己，而更以授其子弘。季龍深恨之，私謂其子邃曰：「主上自都襄國以來，端拱指授，而以吾躬當矢石。二十餘年，南擒劉嶽，北走索頭，東平齊、魯，西定秦、雍，克殄十有三州。成大趙之業者，我也。大單于之望實在於我，而授黃吻婢兒，每一憶此，令人不復能寢食。待主上晏駕之後，不足復留種也。」咸康元年，季龍廢勒子弘，群臣已下勸其稱尊號。季龍下書曰：「王室多難，海陽自棄，四海業重，故免從推逼。朕聞道合乾坤者稱皇，德協人神者稱帝，皇帝之號非所敢聞，且可稱居攝趙天王，以副天人之望。」於是赦其境內，改年曰建武。以夔安為侍中、太尉、守尚書令，郭殷為司空，韓晞為尚書左僕射，魏概、馮莫、張崇、曹顯為尚書，申鐘為侍中，郎闓為光祿大夫，王波為中書令，文武封拜各有差。立其子邃為太子。季龍以讖文天子當從東北來，於是備法駕行自信都而還以應之。分癭陶之柳鄉立停駕縣。

manualTranslations.zh: 勒之居襄國，署為魏郡太守，鎮鄴三台，後封繁陽侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Le resided at Xiangguo, he appointed him Administrator of Wei Commandery, garrisoning Ye's Three Terraces; later he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Le held court at Xiangguo, he named Jilong Administrator of Wei Commandery and posted him to garrison Ye's Three Terraces; later he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 勒即大單于、趙王位，署為單于元輔、都督禁衛諸軍事，遷侍中、開府，進封中山公。
manualTranslations.literal: When Le assumed the titles of Grand Chanyu and Prince of Zhao, he appointed him Chanyu Chief Counselor and Director of All Palace Guard Military Affairs; he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Bearer of the Staff of Office, and advanced to Duke of Zhongshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Le took the titles of Grand Chanyu and Prince of Zhao, he named Jilong Chanyu Chief Counselor and director of palace-guard forces, promoted him to Palace Attendant with an open office, and advanced him to Duke of Zhongshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 及勒僭號，授太尉、守尚書令，進封為王，邑萬戶。
manualTranslations.literal: When Le usurped the imperial title, he granted him Grand Commandant and Acting Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced him to king, with a fief of ten thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Le arrogated an imperial title, he made Jilong Grand Commandant and acting Director of the Masters of Writing, raised him to king, and granted a fief of ten thousand households.

manualTranslations.zh: 季龍自以勳高一時，謂勒即位之後，大單于必在己，而更以授其子弘。
manualTranslations.literal: Jilong considered his merit unmatched in the age and believed that after Le took the throne the title of Grand Chanyu would surely be his; yet it was instead given to Le's son Hong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jilong thought his merit unmatched and assumed that once Le took the throne the Grand Chanyu title would be his—yet Le gave it to his son Hong instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 季龍深恨之，私謂其子邃曰：「主上自都襄國以來，端拱指授，而以吾躬當矢石。
manualTranslations.literal: Jilong deeply resented this and privately told his son Sui: "Since the lord above made Xiangguo his capital, he has sat with folded hands giving orders while I have faced arrows and stones in my own body.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jilong burned with resentment and privately told his son Shi Sui, "Since the lord above made Xiangguo his capital, he has sat back giving orders while I have faced arrows and stones myself.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十餘年，南擒劉嶽，北走索頭，東平齊、魯，西定秦、雍，克殄十有三州。
manualTranslations.literal: For more than twenty years, south capturing Liu Yue, north driving off Suotou, east pacifying Qi and Lu, west settling Qin and Yong, destroying and subduing thirteen provinces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years I captured Liu Yue in the south, drove off the Suotou in the north, pacified Qi and Lu in the east, and settled Qin and Yong in the west, conquering thirteen provinces.

manualTranslations.zh: 成大趙之業者，我也。
manualTranslations.literal: He who completed the enterprise of Great Zhao was I.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am the one who built Great Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 大單于之望實在於我，而授黃吻婢兒，每一憶此，令人不復能寢食。
manualTranslations.literal: The expectation for Grand Chanyu truly rested on me, yet it was given to a yellow-mouthed boy; each time I recall this, it makes one unable again to sleep or eat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Everyone expected me to be Grand Chanyu, yet the title went to a yellow-mouthed boy. Each time I think of it, I cannot sleep or eat.

manualTranslations.zh: 待主上晏駕之後，不足復留種也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wait until after the lord above's death—there will be no need to leave any seed behind."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the lord above dies, there will be no need to leave any of them alive."

manualTranslations.zh: 咸康元年，季龍廢勒子弘，群臣已下勸其稱尊號。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Xian Kang, Jilong deposed Le's son Hong; ministers downward urged him to assume an exalted title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xian Kang 1 (335 CE), Jilong deposed Shi Le's son Hong, and officials from the ministers down urged him to take a loftier title.

manualTranslations.zh: 季龍下書曰：「王室多難，海陽自棄，四海業重，故免從推逼。
manualTranslations.literal: Jilong issued an edict: "The royal house faces many hardships; the Prince of Haiyang abandoned his duties; the burden of the four seas is heavy—therefore I yield to your urging.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jilong issued an edict: "The royal house faces many hardships; the Prince of Haiyang abandoned his duties; the realm's burden is heavy—therefore I yield to your urging.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕聞道合乾坤者稱皇，德協人神者稱帝，皇帝之號非所敢聞，且可稱居攝趙天王，以副天人之望。」
manualTranslations.literal: I have heard that one whose Way matches Heaven and Earth is called huang, and one whose virtue harmonizes people and spirits is called di; the title of emperor I dare not hear—for now I may be called Acting Regent, Heavenly King of Zhao, to answer heaven and men's hopes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that one whose Way matches Heaven and Earth is called huang, and one whose virtue harmonizes people and spirits is called di; the title of emperor I dare not assume—for now call me Acting Regent, Heavenly King of Zhao, to answer heaven and the people's hopes."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是赦其境內，改年曰建武。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he granted amnesty within his borders and changed the era name to Jianwu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed amnesty throughout his realm and changed the era name to Jianwu.

manualTranslations.zh: 以夔安為侍中、太尉、守尚書令，郭殷為司空，韓晞為尚書左僕射，魏概、馮莫、張崇、曹顯為尚書，申鐘為侍中，郎闓為光祿大夫，王波為中書令，文武封拜各有差。
manualTranslations.literal: He appointed Kui An Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and Acting Director of the Masters of Writing; Guo Yin Minister of Works; Han Xi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wei Kai, Feng Mo, Zhang Chong, and Cao Xian Masters of Writing; Shen Zhong Palace Attendant; Lang Kan Supernumerary Grandee; Wang Bo Director of the Palace Secretariat; civil and military enfeoffments and appointments each according to rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kui An became Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and acting Director of the Masters of Writing; Guo Yin Minister of Works; Han Xi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wei Kai, Feng Mo, Zhang Chong, and Cao Xian Masters of Writing; Shen Zhong Palace Attendant; Lang Kan Supernumerary Grandee; Wang Bo Director of the Palace Secretariat; and other civil and military officers received promotions and appointments according to rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 立其子邃為太子。
manualTranslations.literal: He installed his son Sui as crown prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He named his son Shi Sui crown prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 季龍以讖文天子當從東北來，於是備法駕行自信都而還以應之。
manualTranslations.literal: Jilong, because prophetic texts said the Son of Heaven would come from the northeast, thereupon prepared the imperial carriage and traveled from Xindu and back to answer it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because omens said the Son of Heaven would come from the northeast, Jilong staged a full imperial progress from Xindu and back to fulfill the prophecy.

manualTranslations.zh: 分癭陶之柳鄉立停駕縣。
manualTranslations.literal: He divided Willow Township of Yingtao to establish Tingjia County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He carved Willow Township out of Yingtao to establish Tingjia County.

sourceRange.text: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。及蚡死後，切齒追恨。成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。凡此成敗，亦既然矣。苟能易軌，可無覆墜。陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。如此，榮辱何從而生！噂𠴲何辭而起！往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。顛而不扶，焉用彼相！昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。臣若不言，誰當言者！又與冰書曰：君以椒房之親，舅氏之昵，總據樞機，出內王命，兼擁列將州司之位，昆弟網羅，顯布畿甸。自秦、漢以來，隆赫之極，豈有若此者乎！以吾觀之，若功就事舉，必享申伯之名；如或不立，將不免梁竇之跡矣。每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？如此則永保南面之尊，復何黜辱之憂乎！竇武、何進好善虛己。賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。方今四海有倒懸之急，中夏逋僭逆之寇，家有漉血之怨，人有復仇之憾，甯得安枕逍遙，雅談卒歲邪！吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！

manualTranslations.zh: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, when he learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial, saying: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi held power, he submitted a memorial: "I have studied wise and foolish rulers of past ages. When they favored the worthy and elevated them together, the realm rose to peace;

manualTranslations.zh: 若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。
manualTranslations.literal: If they favored kin and the empress's clan, disaster of overthrow and humiliation was sure to follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they favored kin and the empress's clan, overthrow and humiliation were sure to follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Shen Bo of Zhou was called the worthy maternal uncle, because he was enfeoffed outside as a frontier lord and did not hold court power.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shen Bo of Zhou was praised as a worthy maternal uncle because he held a frontier fief and did not grasp court power.

manualTranslations.zh: 降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。
manualTranslations.literal: Descending to King Zhao of Qin, who was enough to be called a fine ruler, he entrusted his two maternal uncles and nearly brought the state to disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even King Zhao of Qin, a capable ruler, trusted his two maternal uncles and nearly ruined the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。
manualTranslations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, who elevated Tian Fen, none of the myriad affairs' essentials went undecided by him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen until every vital decision passed through him.

manualTranslations.zh: 及蚡死後，切齒追恨。
manualTranslations.literal: When Fen died, he gnashed his teeth in later regret.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in bitter regret.

manualTranslations.zh: 成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang sit and take the imperial throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng was weak and could not stand alone; beguiled within by a beautiful consort and indulging the five maternal uncles without, he finally let Wang Mang seize the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！
manualTranslations.literal: Each time one reads these affairs, who does not feel pain and regret!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reading such cases, who does not feel pain and regret!

manualTranslations.zh: 設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。
manualTranslations.literal: Suppose the maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, then one would only hear of two ministers, not two lords.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang or Wang Feng, one would hear of two ministers, not two rulers.

manualTranslations.zh: 若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。
manualTranslations.literal: If they lacked talent, there were the disasters of Dou Xian and Liang Ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they lacked talent, disasters like those of Dou Xian and Liang Ji followed.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡此成敗，亦既然矣。
manualTranslations.literal: All these successes and failures are already thus clear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lesson of these successes and failures is already plain.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
manualTranslations.literal: If one could change course, one could avoid overturn and collapse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side; recalling past affairs, to this day one burns with anguish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.

manualTranslations.zh: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
manualTranslations.literal: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
manualTranslations.literal: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager has died in indignation.

manualTranslations.zh: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
manualTranslations.literal: If the altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would the heart of wolves and jackals be allowed to reach its limit!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Had the altars not been numinous and heaven not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!

manualTranslations.zh: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
manualTranslations.literal: Past affairs are not forgotten, the model for later affairs, yet Directorate Counselor and Left General Yu Bing and others inwardly hold the pivot, outwardly hold supreme command; brothers stand side by side, no minister has a peer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Past affairs are not forgotten, yet Yu Bing as directorate counselor and left general, with his brothers, inwardly holds the pivot and outwardly commands armies, unmatched among ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to withdraw.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his brothers ought to withdraw of their own accord.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with frontier states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in frontier states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此，榮辱何從而生！
manualTranslations.literal: Thus, from what would honor and disgrace arise!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then whence would honor or disgrace arise!

manualTranslations.zh: 噂𠴲何辭而起！
manualTranslations.literal: From what words would slander and calumny spring!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whence would slander spring!

manualTranslations.zh: 往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly there was only Yu Liang alone, long with a name of standing, yet still he brought change to the age; how much more those who hold the posts today, who from the first had no renown!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Yu Liang alone, though long renowned, still brought turmoil; how much more those who hold power today and were never heard of before!

manualTranslations.zh: 且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover human feelings are easily confused and hard to tell door to door; even if Your Majesty today has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Human feelings are easily swayed and cannot be told house to house; even if Your Majesty is impartial, who in the realm will believe it!

manualTranslations.zh: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and name, are far apart in origin and position, and moreover are kin of the state; by reason one ought to yield and rejoice to suit the occasion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bing and I differ in rank and station, yet as kin of the state I ought by rights to yield and rejoice at the occasion.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant alone presses this contrary speech: for Your Majesty above, for Bing's sake below; despising ministers who only accommodate; sitting in judgment of gain and loss.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I speak against the tide alone: for Your Majesty above and for Bing's sake below, hating ministers who only flatter and judging gain and loss plainly.

manualTranslations.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用彼相！
manualTranslations.literal: If one does not right what is overturned, what use is that minister!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and prevention had no gradual steps.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Xu Fu warned against the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not heed him, and loyal ministers became a traitorous house because he did not examine carefully or guard against gradual encroachment.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。
manualTranslations.literal: What your servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What I now set forth is prevention at the first sign.

manualTranslations.zh: 但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Only fearing that Your Majesty may not understand your servant's loyalty and may not use your servant's plan; after the affair has passed, one will again be in the charred wreckage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I fear only that Your Majesty may not see my loyalty or use my plan, and that after disaster passes you will again stand amid the ashes.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang, each time they submitted sealed memorials, never failed to denounce the Wang clan, so both men ended dead or under punishment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang denounced the Wang clan in every sealed memorial and ended dead or punished.

manualTranslations.zh: 谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and did not answer directly, so they preserved themselves and escaped, drawing ridicule from the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and preserved themselves, winning only the age's ridicule.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant wears disheveled hair in a foreign land, holds the rank of supreme general, worries day and night and knows not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣若不言，誰當言者！
manualTranslations.literal: If your servant does not speak, who will speak!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I do not speak, who will!

manualTranslations.zh: 又與冰書曰：君以椒房之親，舅氏之昵，總據樞機，出內王命，兼擁列將州司之位，昆弟網羅，顯布畿甸。
manualTranslations.literal: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of column commanders and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Yu Bing: "By empress kinship and maternal closeness you hold the pivot, issue and receive royal commands, and with your brothers hold command and provincial posts, your network displayed across the capital region.

manualTranslations.zh: 自秦、漢以來，隆赫之極，豈有若此者乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Since Qin and Han, has there been such extreme splendor!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han, has splendor reached such a height!

manualTranslations.zh: 以吾觀之，若功就事舉，必享申伯之名；
manualTranslations.literal: In my view, if merit is achieved and affairs succeed, you will surely enjoy the name of Shen Bo;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In my view, if your work succeeds you will enjoy Shen Bo's fame;

manualTranslations.zh: 如或不立，將不免梁竇之跡矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If not, you will not escape the track of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if not, you will not escape the fate of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.

manualTranslations.zh: 每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。
manualTranslations.literal: Each time I read the histories, rulers never fail to pamper and indulge the maternal clan, letting them hold power and disorder the court; first they have glory beyond the age, then the burden of riding when unfit, the saying that love rightly becomes harm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: History shows that rulers who pamper the maternal clan and let them rule always win brief glory and then the ruin of "love becomes harm."

manualTranslations.zh: 吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？
manualTranslations.literal: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing the first sprout and ending favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I resent that successive rulers never fully guarded against early favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?

manualTranslations.zh: 如此則永保南面之尊，復何黜辱之憂乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Then they would forever preserve the honor of facing south; what worry of dismissal and disgrace!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then they would forever preserve honor facing south, with no fear of dismissal or disgrace!

manualTranslations.zh: 竇武、何進好善虛己。
manualTranslations.literal: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and emptied themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and humbled themselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Worthy men gave them their hearts; though endangered by eunuch minions and mourned by the realm, they could still walk without pride and plotted for the state even at the cost of their lives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Worthy men rallied to them; though eunuchs endangered them and the realm mourned, they could still walk without pride and gave their lives for the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 方今四海有倒懸之急，中夏逋僭逆之寇，家有漉血之怨，人有復仇之憾，甯得安枕逍遙，雅談卒歲邪！
manualTranslations.literal: Now the four seas have the urgency of the inverted hanging; within China flee usurping rebels; families bear blood-soaked grievances and men the regret of vengeance; how can one rest on pillows at ease, discoursing elegantly through the year!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the realm hangs inverted, rebels roam China, families bear blood-soaked grievances and men thirst for vengeance; how can one rest at ease and talk elegantly through the year!

manualTranslations.zh: 吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Though I am few in virtue, I have unduly received the former emperor's grant of command over the columns; with the people of several commanderies I still wish to swallow strong enemies; therefore from recently until now, clashing blades and meeting swords, one season for farming and three for war, yet the army is not exhausted, the granaries have surplus grain, the enemy daily fears us and our borders daily widen; how much more the king's majesty and stately power, how can they be spoken of in the same year!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am little in virtue, yet the former emperor made me a column commander; with several commanderies I still mean to swallow strong foes. From lately until now I farm one season and fight three, yet my armies do not fail, my granaries hold surplus, the enemy daily fears us and our borders widen daily; how much more the majesty of a king and stately power, how can these be compared!"

sourceRange.text: 咸和九年，皝遣其司馬封弈攻鮮卑木堤于白狼，揚威淑虞攻烏丸悉羅侯于平岡，皆斬之。

sourceRange.text: 皝記室參軍封裕諫曰：臣聞聖王之宰國也，薄賦而藏于百姓，分之以三等之田，十一而稅之；寒者衣之，饑者食之，使家給人足。雖水旱而不為災者，何也？高選農官，務盡勸課，人治周田百畝，亦不假牛力；力田者受旌顯之賞，惰農者有不齒之罰。又量事置官，量官置人，使官必稱須，人不虛位，度歲入多少，裁而祿之。供百僚之外，藏之太倉，三年之耕，餘一年之粟。以斯而積，公用于何不足？水旱其如百姓何！雖務農之令屢發，二千石令長莫有志勤在公、銳盡地利者。故漢祖知其如此，以墾田不實，征殺二千石以十數，是以明、章之際，號次升平。自永嘉喪亂，百姓流亡，中原蕭條，千里無煙，饑寒流隕，相繼溝壑。先王以神武聖略，保全一方，威以殄奸，德以懷遠，故九州之人，塞表殊類，繈負萬里，若赤子之歸慈父，流人之多舊土十倍有餘，人殷地狹，故無田者十有四焉。殿下以英聖之資，克廣先業，南摧強趙，東滅句麗，開境三千，戶增十萬，繼武闡廣之功，有高西伯。宜省罷諸苑，以業流人。人至而無資產者，賜之以牧牛。人既殿下之人，牛豈失乎！善藏者藏于百姓，若斯而已矣。邇者深副樂土之望，中國之人皆將壺餐奉迎，石季龍誰與居乎！且魏、晉雖道消之世，猶削百姓不至於七八，持官牛田者官得六分，百姓得四分，私牛而官田者與官中分，百姓安之，人皆悅樂。臣猶曰非明王之道，而況增乎！且水旱之厄，堯、湯所不免，王者宜浚治溝澮，循鄭白、西門、史起溉灌之法，旱則決溝為雨，水則入於溝瀆，上無《雲漢》之憂，下無昏墊之患。句麗、百濟及宇文、段部之人，皆兵勢所徙，非如中國慕義而至，咸有思歸之心。今戶垂十萬，狹湊都城，恐方將為國家深害，宜分其兄弟宗屬，徙于西境諸城，撫之以恩，檢之以法，使不得散在居人，知國之虛實。今中原未平，資畜宜廣，官司猥多，遊食不少，一夫不耕，歲受其饑。必取於耕者而食之，一人食一人之力，游食數萬，損亦如之，安可以家給人足，治致升平！殿下降覽古今之事多矣，政之巨患莫甚於斯。其有經略出世，才稱時求者，自可隨須置之列位。非此已往，其耕而食，蠶而衣，亦天之道也。殿下聖性寬明，思言若渴，故人盡芻蕘，有犯無隱。前者參軍王憲、大夫劉明並竭忠獻款，以貢至言，雖頗有逆鱗，意在無責。主者奏以妖言犯上，至之于法，殿下慈弘苞納，恕其大辟，猶削黜禁錮，不齒於朝。其言是也，殿下固宜納之；如其非也，宜亮其狂狷。罪諫臣而求直言，亦猶北行詣越，豈有得邪！右長史宋該等阿媚苟容，輕劾諫士，己無骨鯁，嫉人有之，掩蔽耳目，不忠之甚。四業者國之所資，教學者有國盛事。習戰務農，尤其本也。百工商賈，猶其末耳。宜量軍國所須，置其員數，已外歸之于農，教之戰法，學者三年無成，亦宜還之于農，不可徒充大員，以塞聰俊之路。臣之所言當也，願時速施行；非也，登加罪戮，使天下知朝廷從善如流，罰惡不淹。王憲、劉明，忠臣也，願宥忤鱗之愆，收其藥石之效。
